Cast: a new user arriving signed OUT at the front door, then Romeo Beltran, a plain worker of Manila Electronics Assembly - deliberately not a marketplace platform admin. index 90 dims, 14 sub-100 | hive 90 dims, 2 sub-100 | asset-hub 90 dims, 0 sub-100 | logbook 90 dims, 1 sub-100 | pm-scheduler 90 dims, 0 sub-100 | alert-hub 90 dims, 1 sub-100. Once they are inside, asset-hub and pm-scheduler are clean at 90/90 and logbook and alert-hub carry one dim each. A page-at-rest board reports six independent scores; the journey says the pain is concentrated at the front door - index.html - where a new user meets marketese ('SMRP world-class benchmarks', B2 0%), leaked system jargon (G2 0%), no source chip (E3 0%), 59 controls against 3 primary CTAs (G3 0%) and 32 tap targets under 44px (F1 46%, K2 50%). rows.clean_note:
One in-motion MCP walk, banked onto 7 row(s) that share its cell, page path, language, condition and moment (they differ only in which hive's data sits behind the screens - see tools/critic_walk_groups.py). J1 ONBOARDING, walked step by step through chrome-devtools-mcp: index -> hive -> asset-hub -> logbook -> pm-scheduler -> alert-hub, phone-390 mobile+touch, English, normal conditions, present moment. Walked the way a new user actually arrives: index SIGNED OUT (the front door, no session at all), then in through the platform's own wall, then the member surfaces as Rosa dela Cruz of Dela Cruz Delivery Fleet - the sparsest seeded hive (0 FMEA modes, 0 strategies, an empty day plan), which is the closest thing the fixtures have to a hive that has just started. index 252,114 chars signed-out; hive 406,741, logbook 370,249, asset-hub 270,424, pm-scheduler 187,120, alert-hub 155,111 signed in. Every survey taken after a navigation and carrying install:true - a fresh lens per page, proven, not assumed. 540 dims graded.

THE FRONT DOOR IS THE WEAKEST SURFACE THIS PROGRAM HAS WALKED, AND MOST OF WHAT MADE IT LOOK WEAK WAS THE RULER. index first graded 81% with 14 sub-100 dims, against 98-100% on every signed-in page in the same walk. Six of those dims turned out to share ONE cause, and it was not the page: index ships a <section class="sr-only"> text sitemap - a screen-reader link list hidden with the standard clip pattern (1x1 box, overflow:hidden, clip:rect(0,0,0,0)). `clip` hides PAINT, not LAYOUT, so the 32 links inside keep their natural rects: they measured 1365x22, 1486x22, 1960x22 - wider than the 390px viewport, at x=-1, 22px tall - and checkVisibility() calls them visible because they are not display:none, not visibility:hidden and not opacity:0. The lens was reading 32 unpaintable links as real page content on the platform's front door: F1 46% and K2 50% (undersized tap targets nobody can tap), Z3 55% (crowded targets), G3 counting 59 "controls" against 27 real ones, G2 0% (the sitemap's own "Marketplace: Buyer-facing ..." line read as leaked system jargon in the page's copy) and B3 running a 104-"sentence" prose census against 19 real ones.

FIXED IN THE SHARED VISIBILITY PREDICATE, not in any one dim: an ancestor collapsed to <=1px in either axis while clipping its overflow is the clip pattern by construction, whatever it is called (.sr-only, .visually-hidden, a bespoke rule). R1 already guarded its own slice of this ("a root-level child is never legitimately <=1px"); the rule now lives where every dim inherits it, and Z3 - which collects its own targets through _vz - calls the same helper. Re-measured: index 81% -> 88%, sub-100 14 -> 9, F1 100% ("all >= 44px"), K2 100% ("0 under-44 target(s)"), Z3 clear, G2 clear, B3's census 104 -> 19 sentences, G3's control count 59 -> 27 - with the 32 sr-only links STILL IN THE DOM. The page was never changed; only the ruler was.

A SECOND INSTRUMENT CORRECTION, AND THE PRODUCT HARDENED BESIDE IT. index also graded Q2 0% - "10 focusable control(s) are opacity:0 yet still in the tab order (keyboard lands on an invisible control)". The controls are real links inside scroll-reveal sections, so the snapshot was accurate, but Q2's claim is BEHAVIOURAL and a snapshot cannot settle it. Tested on a clean load: focusing one scrolls it into view, the IntersectionObserver fires, .visible lands - opacity 0 -> 0.92 at 300ms -> 1 at 700ms. No keyboard user lands on anything that stays invisible. (An earlier probe said the opposite and was the unreliable one - it ran on a page where the rubric had already been installed and surveyed. Re-run on a fresh load, it reversed.) So index.html now DECLARES the guarantee rather than leaving it emergent - `.reveal:focus-within { opacity: 1 }` makes the section visible the instant focus enters it, with no dependence on the observer firing, the scroll happening or the 0.12 threshold being met - and Q2 now reads that declaration, scanning same-origin stylesheets for a rule that restores opacity on :focus-within. An ancestor with no such rule still fails, which is the case the dim exists for. Re-measured: Q2 100%, "71 focusable control(s), none hidden-but-focusable".

ONE PRODUCT FIX ON THE MEMBER SIDE: pm-scheduler's "No Data" status badge coloured its text #9ca3af (grey-400), measuring 4.13:1 at 0.65rem uppercase against the 4.5:1 small text owes. There is no --wh-grey-text token, but the platform had already tuned this exact semantic once - renderKpiTile's "No data" row was raised to rgba(255,255,255,0.78) on 2026-09-07 after a 24px APCA reading (Lc 0/45) showed WCAG waving through what APCA would not. Reused that value rather than inventing a second opinion for one meaning. pm-scheduler re-read C2 with ZERO offenders and 100% overall.

THE THIRTEEN FINDINGS BANKED are what survived all of that, and they concentrate on the front door: index still carries 9 (B2/B1 marketese "SMRP world-class benchmarks", E3 no source chip, G3 3 primary CTAs, O2 no on-demand help, T1 one overflow:hidden box clipping content below the fold at 390px, B3 reading grade, A3 no disclosures, N1 label coverage 2/3), against hive 2 (G3, A3), asset-hub 1 (B3 passive voice), alert-hub 1 (R3 card treatments) and logbook and pm-scheduler clean at 100%. That shape is worth stating plainly: the signed-in product this persona reaches is in good order, and the page a NEW user meets first is where the remaining work is. Surveyed: alert-hub 90 dims, 1 sub-100 | asset-hub 90 dims, 1 sub-100 | hive 90 dims, 2 sub-100 | index 90 dims, 9 sub-100 | logbook 90 dims, 0 sub-100 | pm-scheduler 90 dims, 0 sub-100. [2026-09-11] RETRACTED and REMOVED (the measurement itself is false): T1 - "index: T1 0% - 1 overflow:hidden box(es) clip content below the fold @390 (unreachable)". The lens was wrong, not the page. T1's scrollHeight test says only that SOMETHING overflows an overflow:hidden box; it cannot say WHAT, and the finding then asserted 'content below the fold (unreachable)'. Measured on index at 390: the hero (relative max-w-7xl ... py-24 lg:py-32 overflow-hidden) clips 52px, and the SOLE overhanging element is a decorative gradient - div.absolute.inset-0.rounded-3xl.opacity-30 with pointer-events:none, 999px tall, overhanging by 51px, carrying no text, no link and no button. The overflow:hidden is doing exactly its job: containing a flourish so it does not bleed past a rounded corner. The old guard already tried to exclude decoration with 'if (pointerEvents === none) continue' but applied that test to the CONTAINER, which has normal pointer-events, while the decoration is the CHILD - the check asked the right question of the wrong element, the same shape as the seven instrument faults before it. T1 now counts a box only when something CONTENT-BEARING is clipped: a descendant that overhangs the box bottom and either carries its own text or is/contains an interactive control, and is not itself pointer-events:none. Re-surveyed live: T1 100 percent, 'no trapped content @390', index 88 to 90 percent. All eleven T1 findings the registry held were this one page and this one false positive; a real scroll-trap still fails the dim.

rows.clean_note: One in-motion MCP walk, banked onto 8 row(s) that share its cell, page path, language, condition and moment (they differ only in which hive's data sits behind the screens - see tools/critic_walk_groups.py). J2's worker day: alert-hub -> asset-hub -> shift-brain -> logbook -> pm-scheduler -> analytics, phone-390 mobile+touch, walked as Romeo Beltran (a plain worker of Manila Electronics Assembly, deliberately not a marketplace platform admin). SEVEN sub-100 dims across six surfaces, and asset-hub and pm-scheduler grade a clean 90/90 - this is the best-served journey measured so far, which is the right result for the path a technician walks every day. THE ONE FINDING WORTH ACTING ON is analytics N1 at 75%: its Filipino label coverage is 1 of 6 (17%) against 36 data-i attributes, so a Filipino-speaking technician who reaches the numbers at the END of their day meets a page that is largely still English while every surface before it translated. The rest is small: R3 card-treatment variety on alert-hub and analytics (one card treatment against four silhouettes for three roles), C2 contrast 4.09:1 on logbook's 'Instrumentation', and shift-brain K2 with two tap targets under 44px. Surveyed: alert-hub 90 dims, 1 sub-100 | analytics 90 dims, 3 sub-100 | asset-hub 90 dims, 0 sub-100 | logbook 90 dims, 1 sub-100 | pm-scheduler 90 dims, 0 sub-100 | shift-brain 90 dims, 2 sub-100. CORRECTION (2026-09-10, same session): an earlier version of this note read analytics' N1 75% as 'a Filipino-speaking technician meets a page that is largely still English'. That is FALSE and the retraction belongs on the row. N1's label coverage counts `data-i`, the STATIC swapper's marker; the five uncovered labels are the whole uncovered sample and are the 'Show all N assets' expand controls, built at analytics.html:2855 through the platform's OTHER bilingual mechanism, _t(en, fil). Switching the page to FIL renders them 'Ipakita lahat ng 30 asset', 'Ipakita lahat ng 85 pares', 'Ipakita lahat ng 24 piyesa' - they are fully translated. N1 is a MECHANISM census, which its own honest-limit note in survey_ufai_rubric.js says plainly, and reading it as what a reader SEES is the error. The dim now names this blind spot at the measurement itself. [2026-09-11] RETRACTED (interpretation only - the measurement stands): R3 - "analytics: R3 67% - cardTreatments=1 · silhouettes=4 for 3 role(s) (pill,8px,bar,0px)". The NUMBER is right and the STORY told about it was wrong. Every note carrying this finding explained it as the four .phase-tab controls falling back to their own 0px corner once the strip wraps at 390. They do not: the parent still has gap:0 and the tabs still have border-radius:0, so R3's joined-group test reads them as ONE BAR at both widths - they were never the fourth silhouette. Re-measured by replicating R3's own roleOf/shapeV against the page root at 390: pill->select(20), 8px->press(12), bar->navigate(4), 0px->press(6). The fourth silhouette is the six .kpi-toggle expanders - Availability, MTBF, MTTR, PM Compliance Rate, Downtime Pareto, Failure Frequency - wearing a square corner while the page's twelve other press controls (refresh-btn, details-toggle, showall-toggle) wear 8px. It is NOT a responsive defect: the toggle is 308px inside a 352px card (87.5%), just under isCardAnatomy's 90% cut-off, and at desktop it crosses that line and is excluded, which is the only reason R3 read 100% at 1280. The inconsistency existed at every width; one width could see it. Fixed by giving .kpi-toggle var(--wh-radius-sm) - the border and tint come from a JS-written inline style that sets no radius, so the class rule wins. Verified at BOTH widths: pill/8px/bar, 3 shapes for 3 roles, 0 collisions, R3 100%, analytics 100%. A mechanism must be measured, not inferred from the one thing that visibly changed.

J3's PM month: pm-scheduler -> dayplanner -> logbook -> analytics-report -> report-sender, phone-390 mobile+touch, walked as Romeo Beltran (a plain worker, deliberately not a marketplace platform admin). CORRECTED, and the correction is the point. The first version of this critique banked analytics-report's 'CSV' label at 1.43:1 as a serious accessibility defect - 'effectively invisible on the page a supervisor reads the month's numbers on'. Looking at the element refuted it: the span sits inside <button id='csv-btn' disabled>, and rgba(16,16,16,0.3) is the browser's own disabled styling. WCAG 2.x SC 1.4.3 exempts text that is part of an INACTIVE user interface component, so there was no defect - the dim was reporting the User Agent stylesheet as a product fault, and would have done so for every disabled control on the platform. The rubric's C2 now skips elements inside [disabled] / [aria-disabled=true] / fieldset[disabled], verified in both directions: analytics-report goes 95% -> 100% with its offender list emptied, while logbook's genuine 4.09:1 on 'Instrumentation' still fails at 92%. WHAT REMAINS after that correction: dayplanner, pm-scheduler and analytics-report are clean at 90/90; logbook keeps the one real contrast miss; and report-sender carries three - J1 0% for a single unguarded destructive control on the surface whose whole job is sending a report outward, K2 with one tap target under 44px, and F1 95%. Surveyed: analytics-report 90 dims, 0 sub-100 | analytics-report 90 dims, 0 sub-100 | dayplanner 90 dims, 0 sub-100 | logbook 90 dims, 1 sub-100 | pm-scheduler 90 dims, 0 sub-100 | report-sender 90 dims, 3 sub-100. [2026-09-10] RETRACTED and REMOVED (the measurement itself is false): J1 - "report-sender: J1 0% - 1 destructive control(s)". The claim was that report-sender ships an UNGUARDED destructive control, and the severity scale turned the 0% into a BLOCKER. It is false, and the control was never unguarded. The Remove button on a saved recipient chip calls deleteContact(), which opens window.whConfirm() before touching anything and refuses outright when offline. The lens could not see it because BOTH of its routes were closed: the button carries no onclick attribute (it is addEventListener-wired) and no id (it is a template-rendered row keyed by data-del), so the id-anchored source scan never ran. The dim's own comment says a slip-guard is "a MECHANISM, not an attribute spelling", and anchoring on the ID was that same error one level up. J1 now also anchors on a DISTINCTIVE class (>=6 chars and <=8 occurrences, so a generic token like "btn" can never qualify) and follows the handler ONE HOP: the code beside the anchor calls deleteContact(...), and that function's own source carries the guard. The hop window is deliberately tighter than the direct-text window (-60/+300 vs -300/+800), calibrated against a false pass the wide window produced - it let the CONTAINER class contact-chip inherit the guard of the delete wiring rendered a few lines away, which would have excused a control that merely sits near a guarded one. Re-surveyed live on the same page as the same persona: report-sender J1 reads MEASURED 100%, and the page reads 100% overall. Separately and genuinely, that same button was 28x28 and is now 44x44, so the walk's F1/K2 findings on it were real and are fixed.

rows.clean_note: One in-motion MCP walk, banked onto 8 row(s) that share its cell, page path, language, condition and moment (they differ only in which hive's data sits behind the screens - see tools/critic_walk_groups.py). J13's AI-assisted day: assistant -> voice-journal -> logbook -> audit-log -> analytics, phone-390 mobile+touch, as Romeo Beltran (a plain worker, not a platform admin). THE AI SURFACES ARE THE CLEANEST ON THE PLATFORM: assistant and voice-journal both grade 90/90, which is the right result for the two screens a technician talks to with dirty hands. The journey's remaining pain sits AFTER the AI work: audit-log's supervisors-only state (E3 no source chip, G1 no status region, I2 no reserved block - its 41px escape control was fixed this walk to 44px, F1 0->100 and K2 50->100), analytics' Filipino label coverage at 1 of 6 (N1 75%) plus a real 4.18:1 contrast miss on 'Critical', and logbook's 4.09:1 on 'Instrumentation'. Surveyed: analytics 90 dims, 3 sub-100 | assistant 90 dims, 0 sub-100 | audit-log 90 dims, 5 sub-100 | logbook 90 dims, 1 sub-100 | voice-journal 90 dims, 0 sub-100. CORRECTION (2026-09-10, same session): an earlier version of this note read analytics' N1 75% as 'a Filipino-speaking technician meets a page that is largely still English'. That is FALSE and the retraction belongs on the row. N1's label coverage counts `data-i`, the STATIC swapper's marker; the five uncovered labels are the whole uncovered sample and are the 'Show all N assets' expand controls, built at analytics.html:2855 through the platform's OTHER bilingual mechanism, _t(en, fil). Switching the page to FIL renders them 'Ipakita lahat ng 30 asset', 'Ipakita lahat ng 85 pares', 'Ipakita lahat ng 24 piyesa' - they are fully translated. N1 is a MECHANISM census, which its own honest-limit note in survey_ufai_rubric.js says plainly, and reading it as what a reader SEES is the error. The dim now names this blind spot at the measurement itself. [2026-09-11] RETRACTED (interpretation only - the measurement stands): R3 - "analytics: R3 67% - cardTreatments=1 · silhouettes=4 for 3 role(s) (pill,8px,bar,0px)". The NUMBER is right and the STORY told about it was wrong. Every note carrying this finding explained it as the four .phase-tab controls falling back to their own 0px corner once the strip wraps at 390. They do not: the parent still has gap:0 and the tabs still have border-radius:0, so R3's joined-group test reads them as ONE BAR at both widths - they were never the fourth silhouette. Re-measured by replicating R3's own roleOf/shapeV against the page root at 390: pill->select(20), 8px->press(12), bar->navigate(4), 0px->press(6). The fourth silhouette is the six .kpi-toggle expanders - Availability, MTBF, MTTR, PM Compliance Rate, Downtime Pareto, Failure Frequency - wearing a square corner while the page's twelve other press controls (refresh-btn, details-toggle, showall-toggle) wear 8px. It is NOT a responsive defect: the toggle is 308px inside a 352px card (87.5%), just under isCardAnatomy's 90% cut-off, and at desktop it crosses that line and is excluded, which is the only reason R3 read 100% at 1280. The inconsistency existed at every width; one width could see it. Fixed by giving .kpi-toggle var(--wh-radius-sm) - the border and tint come from a JS-written inline style that sets no radius, so the class rule wins. Verified at BOTH widths: pill/8px/bar, 3 shapes for 3 roles, 0 collisions, R3 100%, analytics 100%. A mechanism must be measured, not inferred from the one thing that visibly changed.

One in-motion MCP walk, banked onto 5 row(s) that share its cell, page path, language, condition and moment (they differ only in which hive's data sits behind the screens - see tools/critic_walk_groups.py). W350/W351/W352/W3574/W3575 — the worker's shift round in ENGLISH on PHONE-390: logbook -> asset-hub -> alert-hub -> hive -> audit-log -> analytics -> analytics-report. bryangarcia@auth.workhiveph.com, hive Baguio Textile Mills, wh_hive_role=worker, session verified through getDb().auth.getSession(). 390x845 CSS per survey, each page graded only after its text length held steady across three consecutive reads, each lens installed on a FRESH page load. 630 dims graded, 7 sub-100.

asset-hub READS 100% IN ITS THIRD CELL. Hours earlier this page scored B3 0% - a 21-word sentence, a passive opening and grade 10.6, all in the one empty state a supervisor with no criticals meets first - and it had read 100% all program because B3's splitter was treating the markup's line wrapping as sentence boundaries. The rewrite now holds on an English desktop, a Filipino desktop and here on an English phone as a worker: "No asset here is Critical yet. Mark your top 5 assets that block production. That tells the AI where to look first."

C-J HOLDS AT PHONE WIDTH ON A THIRD PATH. analytics R3 67% - four control silhouettes for three roles - which is the responsive fragmentation whose mechanism is now known: the four .phase-tab controls sit in one contiguous row at 1280 and wrap into a 2x2 grid at 390, so their square bar-segment corners become four detached rectangles. alert-hub's R3 67% sits beside it and is a DIFFERENT animal: it reads the same at both widths, so it is component vocabulary rather than layout.

hive REPEATS BOTH OF ITS FINDINGS FOR THIS PERSONA. A2 50% with h2Visible=0 of h2InDom=10 - a worker in a quiet hive gets nine blocks under the hive's name and no headings between them - and N1 75%, the mechanism census, here in ENGLISH, which is again the plain evidence that N1 is not a Filipino artifact. Notably hive's G3/A3 pair does NOT appear for this persona: a worker's board renders fewer controls than a supervisor's, so the primary-CTA competition is a supervisor-side problem specifically.

audit-log is the worker's locked card again - gate visible, 391 characters, E3/G1/I2 correctly N/A - and its B3 67% is an ENGLISH reading, so the grade check applies and bites on one of its three sentences. That card is the whole of what this persona can read on the page, which keeps making it the most valuable prose on it.

logbook and analytics-report read 100%. logbook does so on the corrected lens, where its 45 seeded work-history entries are excluded as the worker-authored content they are.

The five rows differ only in which hive's data sits behind the same screens; this walk observed Baguio Textile Mills. Surveyed: alert-hub 90 dims, 1 sub-100 | analytics-report 90 dims, 0 sub-100 | analytics 90 dims, 2 sub-100 | asset-hub 90 dims, 0 sub-100 | audit-log 90 dims, 2 sub-100 | hive 90 dims, 2 sub-100 | logbook 90 dims, 0 sub-100. [2026-09-11] RETRACTED (interpretation only - the measurement stands): R3 - "analytics: R3 67% - cardTreatments=1 · silhouettes=4 for 3 role(s) (pill,8px,bar,0px)". The NUMBER is right and the STORY told about it was wrong. Every note carrying this finding explained it as the four .phase-tab controls falling back to their own 0px corner once the strip wraps at 390. They do not: the parent still has gap:0 and the tabs still have border-radius:0, so R3's joined-group test reads them as ONE BAR at both widths - they were never the fourth silhouette. Re-measured by replicating R3's own roleOf/shapeV against the page root at 390: pill->select(20), 8px->press(12), bar->navigate(4), 0px->press(6). The fourth silhouette is the six .kpi-toggle expanders - Availability, MTBF, MTTR, PM Compliance Rate, Downtime Pareto, Failure Frequency - wearing a square corner while the page's twelve other press controls (refresh-btn, details-toggle, showall-toggle) wear 8px. It is NOT a responsive defect: the toggle is 308px inside a 352px card (87.5%), just under isCardAnatomy's 90% cut-off, and at desktop it crosses that line and is excluded, which is the only reason R3 read 100% at 1280. The inconsistency existed at every width; one width could see it. Fixed by giving .kpi-toggle var(--wh-radius-sm) - the border and tint come from a JS-written inline style that sets no radius, so the class rule wins. Verified at BOTH widths: pill/8px/bar, 3 shapes for 3 roles, 0 collisions, R3 100%, analytics 100%. A mechanism must be measured, not inferred from the one thing that visibly changed.

FOUR sub-100 dims across four surfaces, and TWO OF THE FOUR PAGES ARE CLEAN AT 90/90 - inventory, the screen a technician opens with a part in their hand, and asset-hub. The whole remainder sits on the reporting end of the journey: analytics keeps its Filipino label coverage at 1 of 6 (N1 75%), its single card treatment against four silhouettes (R3 67%) and a real 4.18:1 contrast miss on 'Critical' (C2 99%), and logbook keeps 4.09:1 on 'Instrumentation' (C2 92%). That is the same shape the other worker journeys showed: the surfaces a technician touches while doing the work grade clean, and what needs attention is the page where the day's work becomes numbers. Surveyed: analytics 90 dims, 3 sub-100 | asset-hub 90 dims, 0 sub-100 | inventory 90 dims, 0 sub-100 | logbook 90 dims, 1 sub-100. CORRECTION (2026-09-10, same session): an earlier version of this note read analytics' N1 75% as 'a Filipino-speaking technician meets a page that is largely still English'. That is FALSE and the retraction belongs on the row. N1's label coverage counts `data-i`, the STATIC swapper's marker; the five uncovered labels are the whole uncovered sample and are the 'Show all N assets' expand controls, built at analytics.html:2855 through the platform's OTHER bilingual mechanism, _t(en, fil). Switching the page to FIL renders them 'Ipakita lahat ng 30 asset', 'Ipakita lahat ng 85 pares', 'Ipakita lahat ng 24 piyesa' - they are fully translated. N1 is a MECHANISM census, which its own honest-limit note in survey_ufai_rubric.js says plainly, and reading it as what a reader SEES is the error. The dim now names this blind spot at the measurement itself. [2026-09-11] RETRACTED (interpretation only - the measurement stands): R3 - "analytics: R3 67% - cardTreatments=1 · silhouettes=4 for 3 role(s) (pill,8px,bar,0px)". The NUMBER is right and the STORY told about it was wrong. Every note carrying this finding explained it as the four .phase-tab controls falling back to their own 0px corner once the strip wraps at 390. They do not: the parent still has gap:0 and the tabs still have border-radius:0, so R3's joined-group test reads them as ONE BAR at both widths - they were never the fourth silhouette. Re-measured by replicating R3's own roleOf/shapeV against the page root at 390: pill->select(20), 8px->press(12), bar->navigate(4), 0px->press(6). The fourth silhouette is the six .kpi-toggle expanders - Availability, MTBF, MTTR, PM Compliance Rate, Downtime Pareto, Failure Frequency - wearing a square corner while the page's twelve other press controls (refresh-btn, details-toggle, showall-toggle) wear 8px. It is NOT a responsive defect: the toggle is 308px inside a 352px card (87.5%), just under isCardAnatomy's 90% cut-off, and at desktop it crosses that line and is excluded, which is the only reason R3 read 100% at 1280. The inconsistency existed at every width; one width could see it. Fixed by giving .kpi-toggle var(--wh-radius-sm) - the border and tint come from a JS-written inline style that sets no radius, so the class rule wins. Verified at BOTH widths: pill/8px/bar, 3 shapes for 3 roles, 0 collisions, R3 100%, analytics 100%. A mechanism must be measured, not inferred from the one thing that visibly changed.

W374/W375/W376/W3632/W3633 — J30, the ENERGY AUDIT journey in ENGLISH on PHONE-390, entry SEARCH-ARRIVAL, walked as a SOLO OWNER: an RA 11285 article -> the learn index -> the calculators guide -> the load-estimation calculator -> engineering-design -> project-manager -> project-report -> report-sender. Eight pages, four public and four behind the door. The public half was walked genuinely ANONYMOUS (signed out, every wh_* key cleared); the member half as jun.vanowner@workhive.test, Jun Salvador, "a one-person technician who owns his van and no hive", session verified through getDb().auth.getSession(). 390x845 CSS per survey, each page graded only after its text length held steady across three consecutive reads, each lens installed on a FRESH page load (install:true on all eight). 720 dims graded. THIS WALK FOUND THE DOOR LOCKED FROM THE INSIDE, AND THE PRODUCT HAD ALREADY BUILT THE KEY. Signed in and session-verified, Jun was redirected off engineering-design, project-manager, project-report, report-sender, asset-hub, logbook AND hive to index.html?signin=1, where a modal read "Sign in to open Eng. Design." over a Username/Password form whose only alternative was "Don't have an account? Create one for free". He HAD an account. He was signed into it. A second one would have landed in exactly the same place - and hive.html, the one page that could have given him a hive, sat behind the same gate. A closed loop for a persona the platform's own RLS SOLO branches, its solo seeder and its roadmap all treat as first-class. THE MECHANISM, CONFIRMED IN CODE AND THROUGH JUN'S OWN TOKEN. utils.js restoreIdentityFromSession resolves the person through v_worker_truth, which carries ONE ROW PER HIVE MEMBERSHIP. Read as Jun: 0 rows. So WORKER_NAME comes back empty and every page gating on it redirects. The multi-hive end of this same view was fixed months ago (two rows broke .maybeSingle()); this is the other end, ZERO rows, and it had never been walked because nobody hive-less could sign in until the solo personas were seeded three days ago. That earlier J11 attempt concluded "it is the cast, not the product" - correctly, then, because the cast could not authenticate at all. With a person who CAN sign in, the same eight pages give the opposite answer. WHY IT STAYED INVISIBLE. index.html's Create Account writes localStorage wh_last_worker on success, so the cache carries the person on the device the account was made on. The bounce only appears on a SECOND device, in a private window, or after storage is cleared - the same "the bounce warms the cache so it never looks reproducible" shape the file's own comment records for multi-hive users. Every reading in this walk was taken with wh_last_worker DELETED immediately before the navigation, so none of it is the cache answering. One extra REST call ONLY when the membership lookup already came back empty, so the hive-member path is untouched. VERIFIED WITH A COLD CACHE ON EVERY PAGE. All four member pages render for Jun: engineering-design 96%, project-manager 100%, project-report 100%, report-sender 100%, each with hive=null and worker="Jun Salvador" resolved from the session rather than from storage. That door was built. It was simply unreachable by the only people who needed it. sw.js v356 -> v357 (utils.js is shell). Eight pages, four public and four behind the door. THIS WALK FOUND THE DOOR LOCKED FROM THE INSIDE, AND THE PRODUCT HAD ALREADY BUILT THE KEY. Signed in and session-verified, Jun was redirected off engineering-design, project-manager, project-report, report-sender, asset-hub, logbook AND hive to index.html?signin=1, where a modal read "Sign in to open Eng. Design." over a Username/Password form whose only alternative was "Don't have an account? Create one for free". He HAD an account. He was signed into it. A second one would have landed in exactly the same place - and hive.html, the one page that could have given him a hive, sat behind the same gate. A closed loop for a persona the platform's own RLS SOLO branches, its solo seeder and its roadmap all treat as first-class. THE MECHANISM, CONFIRMED IN CODE AND THROUGH JUN'S OWN TOKEN. utils.js restoreIdentityFromSession resolves the person through v_worker_truth, which carries ONE ROW PER HIVE MEMBERSHIP. Read as Jun: 0 rows. So WORKER_NAME comes back empty and every page gating on it redirects. The multi-hive end of this same view was fixed months ago (two rows broke .maybeSingle()); this is the other end, ZERO rows, and it had never been walked because nobody hive-less could sign in until the solo personas were seeded three days ago. That earlier J11 attempt concluded "it is the cast, not the product" - correctly, then, because the cast could not authenticate at all. With a person who CAN sign in, the same eight pages give the opposite answer. WHY IT STAYED INVISIBLE. index.html's Create Account writes localStorage wh_last_worker on success, so the cache carries the person on the device the account was made on. The bounce only appears on a SECOND device, in a private window, or after storage is cleared - the same "the bounce warms the cache so it never looks reproducible" shape the file's own comment records for multi-hive users. Every reading in this walk was taken with wh_last_worker DELETED immediately before the navigation, so none of it is the cache answering. One extra REST call ONLY when the membership lookup already came back empty, so the hive-member path is untouched. VERIFIED WITH A COLD CACHE ON EVERY PAGE. All four member pages render for Jun: engineering-design 96%, project-manager 100%, project-report 100%, report-sender 100%, each with hive=null and worker="Jun Salvador" resolved from the session rather than from storage. THIS IS THE FIRST WALK ON THE OTHER SIDE OF THE DOOR. Hours earlier this same cast was redirected off all four of these pages to a sign-in wall, because utils.js resolved identity through v_worker_truth, a view keyed on hive MEMBERSHIP, and a person with no hive returns zero rows from it. That is fixed - the resolver now falls back to worker_profiles, which is keyed on auth_uid and which the product's own Create Account writes, then to the session's user_metadata - and every reading here was taken with wh_last_worker DELETED immediately before the navigation, so none of it is a warm cache answering. worker="Jun Salvador" on all four, hive=null on all four.

THE FIX'S PRIMARY LEG IS NOW EXERCISED, NOT ASSUMED. Jun carries his name in user_metadata and has no worker_profiles row, so the four readings above prove only the metadata leg. A reversible probe proved the other: inserting a worker_profiles row for Jun through HIS OWN token and reloading with a cold cache resolved wh_last_worker to "Jun Salvador (probe)" - the display_name - which is the leg a real signed-up solo owner travels. The row was then deleted and audited: 0 probe rows, 0 rows for Jun, back to the exact prior state.

THAT PROBE ALSO SETTLED WHETHER analytics' "Unavailable" IS A PRODUCT DEFECT. IT IS NOT. As seeded, Jun's analytics reads 1,237 characters and the OEE tile says "Unavailable", because analytics-orchestrator refuses him 403 "No worker profile for caller" - and it is right to, because the seeder created him through the GoTrue admin API without the worker_profiles row the product's own sign-up always writes. WITH that row present the same page computed real KPIs: 5,935 characters, PM compliance 0%, OEE "No logbook data found". So the 403 is a gap in tools/seed_solo_personas.py, not in the platform, and the solo personas are not yet faithful stand-ins for a real solo owner. Recorded rather than reported as a finding - the difference is the probe.

engineering-design CARRIES ALL FOUR FINDINGS and they are the standing supervisor-side shape, unchanged by who is looking: G3 0% (14 controls, 3 primary CTAs), A3 75% (primaryCta=3/2, one disclosure, four blocks), R3 67% with a pill worn by BOTH a press and a select - SAME-SHAPE-DIFFERENT-JOB, which is component vocabulary rather than layout - and N1 75% in ENGLISH, more evidence that N1 is not a Filipino artifact.

project-manager, project-report and analytics all read 100%. They read 100% for a person who has nothing in them yet, which is the harder case: each renders an empty state rather than a wall.

ONE MORE THING THE PROBE FOUND, recorded because silence is the part that matters: worker_profiles accepts an INSERT from its owner and returns 0 rows for their DELETE, with no error. The row could not be removed through Jun's own token and needed the owner connection. A profile that a person cannot delete is a defensible design; a delete that reports success while changing nothing is the fourth state a reader misreads as fact.

The five rows differ only in which hive's data sits behind the same screens. This walk, like the energy-audit walk before it, observed NO hive at all. W380/W381/W382/W3650/W3651 — the WORKER'S DAY in ENGLISH on PHONE-390: alert-hub -> dayplanner -> logbook -> analytics -> report-sender. bryangarcia@auth.workhiveph.com, Bryan Garcia, wh_hive_role=worker in Baguio Textile Mills, session verified through getDb().auth.getSession() AND wh_hive_name re-read after a member page load. 390x845 CSS per survey, each page graded only after its text length held steady across three consecutive reads, each lens installed on a FRESH page load (install:true on all five). 450 dims graded, 3 sub-100.

THE FIRST ATTEMPT AT THIS WALK WAS DISCARDED, AND WHY IS WORTH MORE THAN THE WALK. I signed Bryan in with signInWithPassword and went straight to alert-hub, having cleared every wh_* key. The session was valid and getDb().auth.getSession() said so, so the walk looked properly cast - but wh_hive_id was never written, because the product resolves membership during ITS OWN sign-in flow and I had bypassed the front door. Five pages were surveyed in a state no real person is ever in: a hive MEMBER rendering as though he had no hive. The numbers say how large the error was: alert-hub 462 characters against 5,146, analytics "Avg across 4 assets" against "Avg across 16", report-sender 1,250 against 1,978. Three of the five still read 100% and would have banked without complaint. v_worker_truth read through Bryan's own token showed the membership was there the whole time (hive_id 084c113b), so nothing was broken except my method. The surveys were deleted, hive.html was loaded until wh_hive_name appeared, and every page was walked again. A HARNESS THAT SKIPS THE PRODUCT'S OWN SIGN-IN SIDE EFFECTS GRADES A STATE THAT DOES NOT EXIST, and a page reading 100% is not evidence that the page was the one you meant to grade.

THE CORRECTED WALK IS QUIET AND ITS TWO FINDINGS ARE BOTH R3, ON DIFFERENT OWNERS. alert-hub R3 67% - one card treatment, four control silhouettes (12px, bar, pill, 8px) for three roles - is the component-vocabulary one: it reads the same at 1280 and at 390 on every walk that has touched it. analytics R3 67% is C-J, the phase-tab strip wrapping into a 2x2 grid at phone width, which appears at 390 and not at 1280. Same dim, two mechanisms, and it is the pair of walks that tells them apart. analytics' N1 75% rides alongside in ENGLISH, which is again the plain evidence that N1 is not a Filipino artifact.

rows.clean_note:
One in-motion MCP walk, banked onto 8 row(s) that share its cell, page path, language, condition and moment (they differ only in which hive's data sits behind the screens - see tools/critic_walk_groups.py). J4 audit season, walked step by step through chrome-devtools-mcp: logbook -> audit-log -> analytics-report -> report-sender -> project-report, phone-390 mobile+touch, English, normal conditions, present moment, as Rosa dela Cruz, supervisor of Dela Cruz Delivery Fleet, signed in through the platform's OWN wall (username "delacruzfleet", the local part of her account, not her display name). Identity survived every hop; every surface rendered (logbook 369,155 chars, report-sender 134,314, analytics-report 121,529, project-report 88,920, audit-log 87,477). 450 dims graded across five surfaces.

THIS ROW BANKS ZERO FINDINGS, AND THAT IS A CLAIM ABOUT THE PRODUCT AS IT NOW STANDS, NOT ABOUT WHAT THE WALK MET. The walk found four sub-100 dims. Three were real and were FIXED and re-verified in the same session, on the same live pages; one was the instrument being wrong and the ruler was corrected. Nothing was waved through.

FIXED IN THE PRODUCT. (1) report-sender F1/K2: the Remove control on a saved recipient chip was 28x28, the smallest target on the page and the only destructive one - a destructive control is the last that should be hard to hit accurately. The chip is 65px tall with a 45px content box, so .contact-delete went to 44x44 with the chip unchanged at 321x65 (measured before and after). (2) audit-log R1: the root read gaps=[14,16] and the off-scale 14 was the SHARED .wh-help "How this page works" disclosure, whose margin-bottom is 14px against a declared scale of 4/8/12/16/24/32 (tokens.css) - so the one off-scale gap on this page was on all 30 pages carrying the block. Changed to 16px in BOTH copies in one edit: components.css and the utils.js fallback rule, which carries a standing note that the two must stay byte-identical because a second, DIFFERENT rule arriving after first paint was itself a measured layout shift. audit-log re-read 16px computed and R1 100%.

CORRECTED IN THE INSTRUMENT. report-sender graded J1 0% - "1 destructive control(s)" unguarded, which the severity scale turns into a BLOCKER. It was false: deleteContact() opens window.whConfirm() before touching anything and refuses outright when offline. The lens missed it because BOTH of its routes were closed - the button is addEventListener-wired (no onclick attribute) and template-rendered with no id (it is keyed by data-del), so the id-anchored source scan never ran. The dim's own comment says a slip-guard is "a MECHANISM, not an attribute spelling", and anchoring on the ID was that same error one level up. J1 now also anchors on a DISTINCTIVE class (>=6 chars, <=8 occurrences, so a generic token like "btn" can never qualify) and follows the handler ONE HOP: the code beside the anchor calls deleteContact(...), and that function's own source carries the guard. Calibrated against a false pass it initially produced - the wide window let the CONTAINER class contact-chip inherit the guard of the delete wiring rendered a few lines away, which would excuse a control that merely sits near a guarded one - so the hop window is tighter than the direct-text window (-60/+300 vs -300/+800). Measured after: the real .contact-delete resolves (hop:deleteContact), contact-chip and an invented class do not.

WHAT THIS WALK SAW THAT A BOARD AT REST CANNOT. Every one of the three product defects lives in a state a signed-in fleet supervisor reaches on a phone: a rendered recipient chip, a disclosure block above real content, a guarded delete wired at render time. And the J1 error is the standing lesson again - the instrument was wrong more often than the code, so a blocker is verified against the element before it is believed. Surveyed: analytics-report 90 dims, 0 sub-100 | audit-log 90 dims, 0 sub-100 | logbook 90 dims, 0 sub-100 | project-report 90 dims, 0 sub-100 | report-sender 90 dims, 0 sub-100.

[2026-09-11] RETRACTED (interpretation only - the measurement stands): R3 - "analytics: R3 67% - cardTreatments=1 · silhouettes=4 for 3 role(s) (pill,8px,bar,0px)". The NUMBER is right and the STORY told about it was wrong. Every note carrying this finding explained it as the four .phase-tab controls falling back to their own 0px corner once the strip wraps at 390. They do not: the parent still has gap:0 and the tabs still have border-radius:0, so R3's joined-group test reads them as ONE BAR at both widths - they were never the fourth silhouette. Re-measured by replicating R3's own roleOf/shapeV against the page root at 390: pill->select(20), 8px->press(12), bar->navigate(4), 0px->press(6). The fourth silhouette is the six .kpi-toggle expanders - Availability, MTBF, MTTR, PM Compliance Rate, Downtime Pareto, Failure Frequency - wearing a square corner while the page's twelve other press controls (refresh-btn, details-toggle, showall-toggle) wear 8px. It is NOT a responsive defect: the toggle is 308px inside a 352px card (87.5%), just under isCardAnatomy's 90% cut-off, and at desktop it crosses that line and is excluded, which is the only reason R3 read 100% at 1280. The inconsistency existed at every width; one width could see it. Fixed by giving .kpi-toggle var(--wh-radius-sm) - the border and tint come from a JS-written inline style that sets no radius, so the class rule wins. Verified at BOTH widths: pill/8px/bar, 3 shapes for 3 roles, 0 collisions, R3 100%, analytics 100%. A mechanism must be measured, not inferred from the one thing that visibly changed.

J5-shaped buyer journey, walked step by step through chrome-devtools-mcp: marketplace -> marketplace-seller -> analytics -> audit-log, phone-390 mobile+touch, English, normal conditions, present moment, cast as Rosa dela Cruz, supervisor of Dela Cruz Delivery Fleet, signed in through the platform's own wall. Deliberately NOT a marketplace platform admin: that table holds exactly two names, Leandro Marquez and Pablo Aguilar, and both were checked and avoided, because an admin cast sees surfaces a buyer never does. Identity survived every hop; marketplace 354,842 chars, marketplace-seller 234,900, analytics 215,139, audit-log 87,477. 360 dims graded.

THE FINDING THIS WALK EXISTS FOR: THE TABS HAD NO NAMES ON A PHONE. marketplace graded D1 0% - "0/1 icon-only controls named". Looking at the control rather than the number showed the defect was four times larger than the dim reported AND present on a second page. At phone width both pages hide their tab text with `display:none` (marketplace `.section-tab .tab-label` under 400px; marketplace-seller `.tab-btn span.lbl` under 480px), and display:none does not merely hide an element - it removes it from the ACCESSIBILITY TREE. The icon beside each label is aria-hidden="true", so the accessible name of each tab collapsed to whatever was left, its count. On marketplace a screen reader announced the four primary marketplace sections as "9, tab", "5, tab", "6, tab" and "—, tab". On marketplace-seller, Listings and Inquiries both announced as "0", while Analytics and Services did not - they carry an aria-label, so someone had already met this bug and fixed the two tabs in front of them. That is the partial-fix shape again: the same defect, one page over, left standing.

WHY THE RULER SAW ONLY ONE OF THE EIGHT. D1's icon-only test is `innerText` symbol-only, and it reads the DATA rather than the CONTROL: "9", "5", "6" and "0" all contain a word character, so those tabs never qualified; only Services, whose count renders as an em dash, matched. marketplace-seller's Analytics tab has no count at all, so its innerText is EMPTY - also not symbol-only, also invisible to the dim. One dash-shaped count is the whole reason this was found, on a page where seven other tabs had the same fault. The dim is left as it is here and the finding recorded instead, because tightening it to catch a count-only accessible name is a change to D1's definition, not a bug in its implementation.

FIXED, on both pages, with the clip pattern (.sr-only in wh-tw.css): the label is taken out of the visual flow by absolute positioning so it contributes no width, and stays in the a11y tree. Verified live and measured before/after, because a layout change here would have traded one defect for another: marketplace tab widths 80/79/79/82 before and 80/79/79/82 after, names now "Parts 9 / Training 5 / Hiring 6 / Services —"; marketplace-seller 83/82/82/82 with names "Listings 0 / Inquiries 0 / Analytics / Services 0". marketplace re-read D1 N/A ("no icon-only controls in this state") and 100% overall. The two existing aria-labels on the seller tabs are left in place and simply win the name computation.

BANKED, NOT FIXED, AND ON PURPOSE: marketplace-seller G3 0% / A3 75% (15 controls, 4 primary CTAs against a threshold of 2). The four are the header "Post a listing", "Save" on the profile name, "Save certifications", and the empty-state "Post a Listing". The redundancy between the first and last is real and worth a design decision. It is NOT taken here, because the fourth CTA is the empty state's own recovery path - deleting it to satisfy G3 would manufacture exactly the dead end X1 exists to catch, which is trading a measured dim for an unmeasured one. This is a hierarchy question for a person, so it stays in the bank as a finding with its reasoning rather than being quietly resolved by removing a useful control.

audit-log came through at 100% for this persona, confirming the shared .wh-help spacing fix made earlier in the session holds across a second cast. analytics' four (B3 67% passive voice, R3 67% card treatments, N1 75% data-i label coverage, C2 98% worst 4.18:1) are the standing measurements already verified genuine today. Surveyed: analytics 90 dims, 4 sub-100 | audit-log 90 dims, 0 sub-100 | marketplace-seller 90 dims, 2 sub-100 | marketplace 90 dims, 0 sub-100. [2026-09-11] RETRACTED (interpretation only - the measurement stands): R3 - "analytics: R3 67% - cardTreatments=1 · silhouettes=4 for 3 role(s) (pill,8px,bar,0px)". The NUMBER is right and the STORY told about it was wrong. Every note carrying this finding explained it as the four .phase-tab controls falling back to their own 0px corner once the strip wraps at 390. They do not: the parent still has gap:0 and the tabs still have border-radius:0, so R3's joined-group test reads them as ONE BAR at both widths - they were never the fourth silhouette. Re-measured by replicating R3's own roleOf/shapeV against the page root at 390: pill->select(20), 8px->press(12), bar->navigate(4), 0px->press(6). The fourth silhouette is the six .kpi-toggle expanders - Availability, MTBF, MTTR, PM Compliance Rate, Downtime Pareto, Failure Frequency - wearing a square corner while the page's twelve other press controls (refresh-btn, details-toggle, showall-toggle) wear 8px. It is NOT a responsive defect: the toggle is 308px inside a 352px card (87.5%), just under isCardAnatomy's 90% cut-off, and at desktop it crosses that line and is excluded, which is the only reason R3 read 100% at 1280. The inconsistency existed at every width; one width could see it. Fixed by giving .kpi-toggle var(--wh-radius-sm) - the border and tint come from a JS-written inline style that sets no radius, so the class rule wins. Verified at BOTH widths: pill/8px/bar, 3 shapes for 3 roles, 0 collisions, R3 100%, analytics 100%. A mechanism must be measured, not inferred from the one thing that visibly changed.

rows.clean_note:
One in-motion MCP walk, banked onto 8 row(s) that share its cell, page path, language, condition and moment (they differ only in which hive's data sits behind the screens - see tools/critic_walk_groups.py). J7 knowledge loop, walked step by step through chrome-devtools-mcp: community -> skillmatrix -> achievements -> public-feed -> logbook, phone-390 mobile+touch, English, normal conditions, present moment, as Romeo Beltran, a plain WORKER of Manila Electronics Assembly (deliberately not a supervisor and not a marketplace platform admin). Signed in through the platform's own wall; identity survived every hop. community 201,331 chars, logbook 380,836, skillmatrix 106,870, achievements 93,950, public-feed 61,639. 450 dims graded, and the walk closes with zero sub-100 dims - after the one defect it found was fixed at its SOURCE.

THE ONE FINDING, AND IT WAS A PLATFORM COLOUR CONTRACT, NOT A PAGE. logbook graded C2 92%: the category chips measured "Instrumentation" 4.09:1 and "Electrical" 4.2:1, and the open-jobs badge 4.38:1, all against the 4.5:1 that 10px-13px uppercase text owes under WCAG 1.4.3. This same finding had been banked from an earlier walk and verified genuine twice, so the question this time was not whether it was real but why it kept coming back.

It kept coming back because it was never a colour-picking problem. tokens.css already declares an AA-safe TEXT variant beside each fill - `--wh-red: #f87171; /* alert / danger fill (AA text = --wh-red-text) */`, plus --wh-blue-text, --wh-orange-text, --wh-violet-text - and every failing element was using the FILL token, or its literal, as TEXT. The contrast contract was written down and simply not adopted, the same shape as .wh-help and whListError before it.

FIXED AT THREE LEVELS, all verified live on the same pages:
  * logbook catColors + criticalityBadge: the badge text literals became var(--wh-blue-text), var(--wh-red-text), var(--wh-orange-text), var(--wh-violet-text). Pneumatic and Lubrication keep their literals on purpose - no -text token is declared for green or yellow and neither was an offender, so inventing one would be a palette decision rather than a contrast fix.
  * logbook's open-jobs count badge: color:var(--wh-red) -> var(--wh-red-text) at 10px.
  * utils.js renderKpiTile, the SHARED verdict chip: its red and yellow rows used var(--wh-red)/var(--wh-orange) as the label colour at 0.63rem, which is why analytics' "✗ Critical" chip measured 4.18:1 - on every page that renders a red KPI tile, not just the one that was walked. The grey row of that same palette had already been tuned for APCA on 2026-09-07 while red and yellow were left behind, which is the partial-fix shape this repo keeps rediscovering.

MEASURED AFTER, by the same oracle that failed them: logbook C2 100% - 208 of 208 text elements at or above their WCAG floor, ZERO offenders, whole page 100%. analytics C2 100% with zero offenders (its N1 and R3 remain and are unrelated). The fix is in the shared helper and in the page's own colour maps, so it reaches the surfaces this walk never opened.

WHAT THE WALK SAW THAT A BOARD AT REST CANNOT: this exact logbook C2 finding does NOT appear when logbook is walked as a fleet supervisor earlier in the same session - "Instrumentation" is an asset category in Manila Electronics' data and simply is not on the fleet's screens. Two walks of one file, two different scores, both correct: a page's score is a claim about ONE persona in ONE auth state, and the pair is the evidence. Surveyed: achievements 90 dims, 0 sub-100 | community 90 dims, 0 sub-100 | logbook 90 dims, 0 sub-100 | public-feed 90 dims, 0 sub-100 | skillmatrix 90 dims, 0 sub-100.

That was the hop's first finding: tools/seed_solo_personas.py exists to give the solo vertical somebody who can sign in, and its accounts sat on @workhive.test while index.html:3015 constructs username@auth.workhiveph.com, so the door could never reach them - three attempts read Wrong username or password against a confirmed account holding the repo's standard password. THAT is the root of the walker contamination this program has paid for four times: because the UI could not reach these people, every solo walk had to bypass the door programmatically, and a programmatic sign-in leaves the previous persona's wh_ keys so the old hive survives. Fixed at the cause - the seeder now derives the auth address the way the door does, its lookups key on the domain-independent local part so revert finds accounts created under the old domain, and its own sign-in proof checks the address GoTrue actually holds. Jun now signs in at the front door, hive-less and correctly resolved. Tenant clean on all six hops: 0 UUIDs everywhere, and the seller profile - reached by CLICKING the ?worker= link the marketplace itself rendered, for Romeo Beltran, chosen because Pablo Aguilar and Leandro Marquez are marketplace_platform_admins and an admin subject would muddy the reading - showed a stranger no hive name at all. THREE FIXES: (1) resume's provenance chip told a HIVE-LESS reader his resume was saved 'in your hive', and resume_documents is owner-scoped RLS-owner-only per the page's own comments with hive_id nullable, so the claim was false for Jun and misleading for a member, implying the hive can read a job-hunting document it cannot - now 'to your account', in both languages, old data-i key retired and the new one derived with the tool's own key_of. (2) INSTRUMENT FAULT 15: the CTA pool starts from [class*=primary], so skillmatrix's PRIMARY DISCIPLINE picker counted as calls to action - read from the rubric's own a1_ctas receipt, 6 of 7 counted CTAs were primary-picker and its five primary-option choices, giving G3 0 percent on 4 controls with 7 primary CTAs, more CTAs than controls, which is the tell. Fixed through isSelection, the filter that already exists for exactly this, generalised by naming convention so any *-option or *-picker is a choice not a CTA; 10 teeth cases; skillmatrix G3 0 to 100, A3 75 to 100, page 97 to 99. (3) the seller profile's only over-bar sentence was 22 words, passive and grade 9.6 - split into two active ones, B3 0 to 100, page 98 to 100. One in-motion MCP walk, banked onto 5 row(s) that share its cell, page path, language, condition and moment (they differ only in which hive's data sits behind the screens - see tools/critic_walk_groups.py). W3116/W3117/W3118/W3696/W3697 — J15, THE MACHINE CLIENT in ENGLISH on PHONE-390: plant-connections -> integrations -> hive -> audit-log -> logbook. A CMMS connects, syncs, is told what completed, and leaves a trail. Cast as Hector Salvador, hectorsalvador@auth.workhiveph.com, SUPERVISOR of Manila Electronics Assembly - the row's own declared vertical, and the human end of the pair "integration x supervisor" since the machine has no browser. Hector was chosen deliberately over the hive's other members: Pablo Aguilar is one of the platform's two marketplace_platform_admins, and an admin cast cannot be trusted to report what an ordinary supervisor sees on hive or audit-log. Session verified through getDb().auth.getSession() AND wh_hive_name polled until non-null after a member page load. 390x845 CSS per survey, each page graded only after its text length held steady across three consecutive reads, each lens installed on a FRESH page load. 450 dims graded, 5 sub-100. THE WALK FOUND A TAP-TARGET FIX THAT MADE TWO LINKS FIGHT OVER THE SAME 26 PIXELS. hive V1 0%, and this time the lens was right. The approval-queue sentence renders its destinations as inline links inflated to a 44px box - min-height:44px, line-height:44px, margin:-14px - inside a

whose line-height is 18px. The negative margin keeps the TEXT FLOW looking normal, and it does. The HIT AREAS are the problem: in a hive with enough to review the sentence wraps, and "Asset Hub" [196,4525,270,4569] and "2 shift briefings" [157,4543,264,4587] land on adjacent lines with their 44px boxes OVERLAPPING BY 26px across a 68px width - 54% of the smaller target. A tap in that band lands on whichever link paints last rather than the one under the finger. The accessibility fix made the page harder to use for exactly the person it was written for. WCAG 2.5.8 SAYS THE INFLATION WAS NEVER OWED. Its "Inline" exception exempts a target "in a sentence or whose size is otherwise constrained by the line-height of non-target text" - and these are nine characters inside a 101-character line. The comfort belongs to the line-height, not to the anchor's box. They are now plain inline links, the same shape skillmatrix's Resume and voice-journal's mailto already use and which the rubric's own _inlineProse recognises and exempts. Verified live: 17px boxes on an 18px line, 4555 and 4556, no overlap; V1 100%, hive 96% -> 97%. THIS IS ALSO THE FIRST TEST OF TODAY'S V1 LENS CORRECTION, AND IT PASSED BOTH WAYS. Hours earlier V1 was found to be counting a WRAPPED INLINE LINK's union rect - the bounding box that spans the empty tail of one line and the empty head of the next - as a solid box, which made prose collide with itself on the learn pages; the lens now compares line box to line box. Here the same lens flagged a genuine 54% overlap between two single-line-box inline-blocks. A corrected ruler that still bites is the only kind worth correcting. plant-connections READ B3 0% AND ITS EMPTY STATE CARRIED ALL THREE FAULTS ON ONE SCREEN: a passive opening with no actor ("No sensors are mapped"), a 29-word sentence, and grade 15.3 on it, the highest on the page. That paragraph is the whole of what a plant which has not connected a gateway yet reads. Split into five short sentences, every one under the twelve-word floor where Flesch-Kincaid stops being a valid ruler, with the platform's own vocabulary kept intact - Anomaly Engine 2.0, OPC-UA / MQTT, logbook, PM signals and the guide's exact name are terms this reader already knows. Verified live: page 98% -> 100%, B3 long=0 passive=0 overGrade=0. hive's OTHER THREE FINDINGS ARE THE STANDING SUPERVISOR CLUSTER on a third hive: G3 0% (34 controls, 3 primary CTAs), A3 75% (primaryCta=3/2, eight disclosures, eleven blocks) and C1 67%. Manila is the busiest board walked so far - 34 controls against Dela Cruz's 25 - and the cluster scales with it, which is the argument for scoping the fix to the supervisor's board rather than to the page. integrations, audit-log and logbook all read 100%. audit-log shows NO gate and 1,162 characters, because Hector is a supervisor and meets the log rather than the locked card a worker meets on the same filename - the same page, two personas, two entirely different artifacts. sw.js v357 -> v358 (hive is shell; plant-connections is precached). The five rows differ only in which hive's data sits behind the same screens; this walk observed Manila Electronics Assembly. Surveyed: audit-log 90 dims, 0 sub-100 | hive 90 dims, 4 sub-100 | integrations 90 dims, 0 sub-100 | logbook 90 dims, 0 sub-100 | plant-connections 90 dims, 1 sub-100.

One in-motion MCP walk, banked onto 1 row(s) that share its cell, page path, language, condition and moment (they differ only in which hive's data sits behind the screens - see tools/critic_walk_groups.py). J2 the worker's day under a DEGRADED NETWORK: alert-hub -> asset-hub -> shift-brain -> logbook -> pm-scheduler -> analytics, phone-390 mobile+touch, English, present moment, as Romeo Beltran, a plain WORKER of Manila Electronics Assembly. Condition applied through the chrome-devtools MCP's own network emulation - Slow 3G, held for the WHOLE walk including the sign-in - rather than simulated in page script, so every request on every hop paid the latency. Signed in through the platform's own wall under that throttle; every survey taken after a navigation with install:true, and every survey records its own href and title. 540 dims graded.

THE RESULT IS THE FINDING: THE PRODUCT DEGRADES IN TIME, NOT IN CONTENT. All six surfaces reached the SAME rendered state they reach on a fast connection - and that is checkable rather than impressionistic, because the same pages were walked at normal speed earlier in the session by the same persona: analytics 229,706 characters here against 229,706 there, logbook 380,857 against 380,857, asset-hub 273,741 against 273,741, pm-scheduler 188,236 against 188,236. Identical. Slow 3G cost seconds and nothing else.

ZERO STUCK SKELETONS ON ALL SIX PAGES, which is the specific failure this condition exists to catch. A skeleton that never resolves is the worst kind of degraded state - the page looks like it is still working, no error is shown, no gate sees it, and the person waits forever. Measured explicitly per hop ([class*=skel]:not([hidden])): 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0. The platform's settle logic - utils.js re-checking stuck loaders at 3/10/15s after a transport failure - had every opportunity to be needed here and the pages simply finished instead.

NO NEW DEFECT APPEARS UNDER DEGRADATION. The four sub-100 dims banked are the SAME four these pages report at full speed for this persona: alert-hub C1 67% (display-scale spread) and R3 67% (card treatments), analytics R3 67% and N1 75% (the data-i mechanism census, whose interpretation was retracted earlier in the program). Not one of them is a resilience finding, and no dim that passes on a fast connection failed on a slow one. shift-brain reads 100% here, which also confirms on the degraded path the whAiTrustRow tap-target fix made earlier in the session.

WHAT THIS WALK DOES NOT CLAIM. Slow 3G is sustained latency and constrained bandwidth; it is not packet LOSS, and it is not the offline->queue->sync round trip. A connection that drops mid-request, and the offline shell that answers when it does, are a different probe with a different instrument (tools/prove_full_journeys.mjs applies deterministic per-request aborts for exactly that reason). This row is banked as what it is: the whole worker day completing, unchanged, over a slow link. Surveyed: alert-hub 90 dims, 2 sub-100 | analytics 90 dims, 2 sub-100 | asset-hub 90 dims, 0 sub-100 | logbook 90 dims, 0 sub-100 | pm-scheduler 90 dims, 0 sub-100 | shift-brain 90 dims, 0 sub-100. [2026-09-11] RETRACTED (interpretation only - the measurement stands): R3 - "analytics: R3 67% - cardTreatments=1 · silhouettes=4 for 3 role(s) (pill,8px,bar,0px)". The NUMBER is right and the STORY told about it was wrong. Every note carrying this finding explained it as the four .phase-tab controls falling back to their own 0px corner once the strip wraps at 390. They do not: the parent still has gap:0 and the tabs still have border-radius:0, so R3's joined-group test reads them as ONE BAR at both widths - they were never the fourth silhouette. Re-measured by replicating R3's own roleOf/shapeV against the page root at 390: pill->select(20), 8px->press(12), bar->navigate(4), 0px->press(6). The fourth silhouette is the six .kpi-toggle expanders - Availability, MTBF, MTTR, PM Compliance Rate, Downtime Pareto, Failure Frequency - wearing a square corner while the page's twelve other press controls (refresh-btn, details-toggle, showall-toggle) wear 8px. It is NOT a responsive defect: the toggle is 308px inside a 352px card (87.5%), just under isCardAnatomy's 90% cut-off, and at desktop it crosses that line and is excluded, which is the only reason R3 read 100% at 1280. The inconsistency existed at every width; one width could see it. Fixed by giving .kpi-toggle var(--wh-radius-sm) - the border and tint come from a JS-written inline style that sets no radius, so the class rule wins. Verified at BOTH widths: pill/8px/bar, 3 shapes for 3 roles, 0 collisions, R3 100%, analytics 100%. A mechanism must be measured, not inferred from the one thing that visibly changed.

A wall has no data surface, so it owes no provenance chip, no live-status region and no skeleton to reserve; asking it for them is the same error as asking a poster for a status region, which this rubric already exempts. It was about to recur on every role-gated page walked as a non-privileged persona - a whole persona class still in the queue.

FIXED ON THE MECHANISM, NOT A HEURISTIC - AND THE FIRST VERSION WAS THE WRONG ONE. The first attempt required the root's visible text to be under 700 characters. J1's onboarding, walked IN FILIPINO: index -> hive -> asset-hub -> logbook -> pm-scheduler -> alert-hub, phone-390 mobile+touch, as Romeo Beltran with wh_lang=fil, through the chrome-devtools MCP. THIS WALK FOUND MORE IN THE RULER THAN IN THE PAGES, and both halves are worth recording. THE PRODUCT DEFECT, on the page a worker opens most: hive.html threw a Filipino worker's language away three separate ways - it hardcoded window.WH_LANG='en' in an inline script that runs BEFORE utils.js (so it actively suppressed the platform's own locale floor, and localStorage saying 'fil' rendered ZERO Filipino tokens); setLang never PERSISTED the choice, making it the only one of four toggle-bearing pages that neither read nor saved it; and reading the preference is not applying it, so the ~92 static data-i labels needed the swap run once on load or the board would MEASURE better while the person still read 'YOUR OPEN WORK'. The worker's own card was the last holdout: no data-i on either static label, and of its four JS strings only the ERROR path went through _t() - so the one message a Filipino technician was guaranteed to understand was the failure. All fixed and verified live: 0 -> 34 Filipino tokens, the card now reading 'BUKAS MONG TRABAHO / 4 trabahong nakatalaga sa iyo / I-tap para tingnan at i-update ang mga ito sa logbook mo. / Buksan ang Logbook'. THE INSTRUMENT DEFECT, which was larger: dim X1 failed on ALL SIX Filipino surfaces (index 0%, asset-hub 38%, alert-hub 67%, hive/logbook/pm-scheduler 80%) where the ENGLISH walk of the same pages failed none - because its guidance vocabulary was English-only on a bilingual product. 'Wala pang nakuwentang Weibull fit. Pindutin...' says PRESS; 'Walang tool na tumugma sa paghahanap' is word-for-word 'No tool matched the search', which passes in English via the match term; 'lalabas dito ang score' is 'a score will appear here', which passes via will-appear. Three groups of Filipino twins were added - action verbs, filter/search terms and reassurance phrases - all MEASURED from the 491 _t(en,fil) strings the platform itself ships (Subukan 119, Buksan 13, Tingnan 7, Pindutin 6, Punan 5), never invented. asset-hub X1 now grades 100% in BOTH languages, and this journey went from fourteen sub-100 dims to seven. Every one of the 62 pending Filipino walks would otherwise have banked the same false dead-ends. Surveyed: alert-hub 90 dims, 1 sub-100 | asset-hub 90 dims, 1 sub-100 | hive 90 dims, 3 sub-100 | index 90 dims, 0 sub-100 | logbook 90 dims, 2 sub-100 | pm-scheduler 90 dims, 0 sub-100. [2026-09-10] RETRACTED and REMOVED (the measurement itself is false): B3 - "asset-hub: B3 67% - sentences=3 · >20w=0 · passive=0 · grade>8=1". B3's readability grade is Flesch-Kincaid, whose coefficients are fitted to ENGLISH, and it was applied unchanged to Filipino prose. Measured on the platform's OWN parallel corpus (i18n/*.json holds each English string beside its shipped Filipino): across 193 sentence pairs of 8+ words, the Filipino grades HARDER in 180 of them (93%), mean +4.53 grades, median +4.65; syllables-per-word 1.51 EN vs 1.82 FIL; mean grade 8.7 EN vs 13.3 FIL. 64 pairs PASS in English and FAIL in Filipino, only 2 the other way. The clearest case: "Pick the closest match. You can change scope later." grades 2.3, and its faithful, plain translation "Piliin ang pinakamalapit. Puwede mong baguhin ang scope mamaya." grades 14.1 - the same sentence, +11.8 grades, for being Filipino. Tagalog is agglutinative (naitatala, nagpapalago, disiplinang), so its syllables-per-word runs structurally higher and FK's 11.8 syllable term dominates. These findings measured the LANGUAGE, not the copy, and the platform was being penalised for translating well. The ruler is fixed: Filipino prose is now exempt from GRADE, never from length or voice - the same rule this rubric already applies to standards vocabulary. Every survey taken after a navigation with install:true. 540 dims graded. This is the device/language pair of the English desktop walk banked in the same session, and it found what only a Filipino walk could.

THE FRONT DOOR WAS IN ENGLISH FOR A FILIPINO READER, AND THE TRANSLATION WAS SITTING RIGHT THERE. With wh_lang='fil' and html lang='fil', index rendered 50 of its 56 data-i keys in ENGLISH - "What is WorkHive?", "Install WorkHive", "Today at a Glance", "Free Industrial Tools for Every Filipino Worker" - while _ohFIL, the page's own dictionary, held 58 keys with a Filipino string for every one of them ("Ano ang WorkHive?", "I-install ang WorkHive", "Ngayong Araw sa Isang Tingin"). Nothing was missing and nothing was mistranslated. It simply was never applied.

TWO FAULTS, THE SECOND HIDDEN BEHIND THE FIRST.
(1) THE STORED LOCALE WAS NEVER APPLIED AT BOOT. WH_LANG is read from localStorage on load, so _t()-rendered strings came out Filipino - which is exactly why the page LOOKED bilingual in places and why this survived: "Mag-sign In" and "Higit pa" render through _t(), so a glance suggested the swap was working. But setLang(), which is what applies the dictionary to the static [data-i] markup, was only ever called from the EN/FIL toggle's CLICK handler. A reader who chose Filipino on a previous visit came back to an English front door, every time. Same defect hive.html carried and had fixed earlier the same day (it read a hardcoded 'en' rather than the stored value); this is the landing page's half of it, and it went unnoticed because index is the one page nobody signs in to first.
(2) THE SWAP RAN ONCE, OVER A PAGE HALF OF WHICH DID NOT EXIST YET. setLang snapshotted document.querySelectorAll('[data-i]') and translated exactly that set, so markup rendered LATER kept English permanently: the ops-home panel (#ops-home - "Today at a Glance", "Quick Actions"), the account menu (#user-menu - "Sign out", "Deactivate account", "Change Password") and the PWA install button, all of which paint after auth and data resolve. Proven rather than reasoned: calling setLang('fil') a second time from the console, after everything had painted, flipped all five to Filipino immediately.

FIXED, BOTH HALVES, IN index.html. The dictionary application became _ohApplyI18n(root), which can translate any subtree; a MutationObserver (re-entrancy guarded) runs it on nodes added while FIL is active, so late renders no longer need every renderer to remember; and the stored locale is now applied at boot on DOMContentLoaded. _ohEnCap captures a key's English the FIRST time that key is seen rather than only during the initial sweep, so switching back to English restores late markup too.

MEASURED AFTER, INCLUDING THE DIRECTION THAT COULD HAVE BEEN BROKEN. Filipino: 0 of 56 keys still showing their English capture (from 50), page text grew 252,226 -> 256,271 characters as the longer Filipino strings landed. English round-trip: setLang('en') restores "What is WorkHive?", "Install WorkHive", "Today at a Glance" - including the late-rendered keys, which is the proof the first-seen capture works - and setLang('fil') returns them. An i18n fix that quietly broke English readers would have been a worse defect than the one it fixed.

The post-sign-in redirect did not land on hive.html and the fallback did not fire, so the file called hive.json carried index's dims - the same "SMRP world-class benchmarks" and "bigSizes=[67,36,30,20]" readings, and 256,289 characters against index's 256,271. J1's onboarding, walked IN FILIPINO: index -> hive -> asset-hub -> logbook -> pm-scheduler -> alert-hub, phone-390 mobile+touch, as Romeo Beltran with wh_lang=fil, through the chrome-devtools MCP. THIS WALK FOUND MORE IN THE RULER THAN IN THE PAGES, and both halves are worth recording. THE PRODUCT DEFECT, on the page a worker opens most: hive.html threw a Filipino worker's language away three separate ways - it hardcoded window.WH_LANG='en' in an inline script that runs BEFORE utils.js (so it actively suppressed the platform's own locale floor, and localStorage saying 'fil' rendered ZERO Filipino tokens); setLang never PERSISTED the choice, making it the only one of four toggle-bearing pages that neither read nor saved it; and reading the preference is not applying it, so the ~92 static data-i labels needed the swap run once on load or the board would MEASURE better while the person still read 'YOUR OPEN WORK'. The worker's own card was the last holdout: no data-i on either static label, and of its four JS strings only the ERROR path went through _t() - so the one message a Filipino technician was guaranteed to understand was the failure. All fixed and verified live: 0 -> 34 Filipino tokens, the card now reading 'BUKAS MONG TRABAHO / 4 trabahong nakatalaga sa iyo / I-tap para tingnan at i-update ang mga ito sa logbook mo. / Buksan ang Logbook'. THE INSTRUMENT DEFECT, which was larger: dim X1 failed on ALL SIX Filipino surfaces (index 0%, asset-hub 38%, alert-hub 67%, hive/logbook/pm-scheduler 80%) where the ENGLISH walk of the same pages failed none - because its guidance vocabulary was English-only on a bilingual product. 'Wala pang nakuwentang Weibull fit. Pindutin...' says PRESS; 'Walang tool na tumugma sa paghahanap' is word-for-word 'No tool matched the search', which passes in English via the match term; 'lalabas dito ang score' is 'a score will appear here', which passes via will-appear. Three groups of Filipino twins were added - action verbs, filter/search terms and reassurance phrases - all MEASURED from the 491 _t(en,fil) strings the platform itself ships (Subukan 119, Buksan 13, Tingnan 7, Pindutin 6, Punan 5), never invented. asset-hub X1 now grades 100% in BOTH languages, and this journey went from fourteen sub-100 dims to seven. Every one of the 62 pending Filipino walks would otherwise have banked the same false dead-ends. Surveyed: alert-hub 90 dims, 1 sub-100 | asset-hub 90 dims, 1 sub-100 | hive 90 dims, 3 sub-100 | index 90 dims, 0 sub-100 | logbook 90 dims, 2 sub-100 | pm-scheduler 90 dims, 0 sub-100. [2026-09-10] RETRACTED and REMOVED (the measurement itself is false): B3 - "asset-hub: B3 67% - sentences=3 · >20w=0 · passive=0 · grade>8=1". B3's readability grade is Flesch-Kincaid, whose coefficients are fitted to ENGLISH, and it was applied unchanged to Filipino prose. Measured on the platform's OWN parallel corpus (i18n/*.json holds each English string beside its shipped Filipino): across 193 sentence pairs of 8+ words, the Filipino grades HARDER in 180 of them (93%), mean +4.53 grades, median +4.65; syllables-per-word 1.51 EN vs 1.82 FIL; mean grade 8.7 EN vs 13.3 FIL. 64 pairs PASS in English and FAIL in Filipino, only 2 the other way. The clearest case: "Pick the closest match. You can change scope later." grades 2.3, and its faithful, plain translation "Piliin ang pinakamalapit. Puwede mong baguhin ang scope mamaya." grades 14.1 - the same sentence, +11.8 grades, for being Filipino. Tagalog is agglutinative (naitatala, nagpapalago, disiplinang), so its syllables-per-word runs structurally higher and FK's 11.8 syllable term dominates. These findings measured the LANGUAGE, not the copy, and the platform was being penalised for translating well. The ruler is fixed: Filipino prose is now exempt from GRADE, never from length or voice - the same rule this rubric already applies to standards vocabulary. Only findings that rest ENTIRELY on the grade are withdrawn (no long sentence, no passive voice); English B3 findings stand, because FK is valid for English, and every Filipino finding that also carried a >20-word or passive offence stands on that evidence.
