One in-motion MCP walk, banked onto 3 row(s) that share its cell, page path, language, condition and moment (they differ only in which hive's data sits behind the screens - see tools/critic_walk_groups.py). J30, THE ENERGY AUDIT, walked in FILIPINO at desktop-1280: the RA 11285 article -> the learn hub -> the calculators article -> the load-estimation calculator -> engineering-design -> project-manager -> project-report -> report-sender. Christine Dizon, christinedizon@auth.workhiveph.com, supervisor of Lucena Pharmaceutical Mfg., wh_lang=fil, session verified and wh_hive_name polled until non-null. Eight pages, each graded only after its text length held steady AND no visible loader element remained, each lens installed on a FRESH load with install:true asserted. Viewport read back as 1280x860 CSS.

THE CONTENT LAYER IS THE MONOLINGUAL SEAM IN AN OTHERWISE BILINGUAL PLATFORM, and this journey crosses the seam twice. Every page whose own lang declaration says "fil" reads 100%: engineering-design 1,889 chars, project-manager 1,759, project-report 1,482, report-sender 2,109, and the learn HUB 99% at 3,324. Every page whose lang says "en" is a learn ARTICLE and reads 89-90% with seven to nine failing dims: ra-11285 90% at 15,867 characters, free-engineering-calculators 89% at 14,873. The load-estimation calculator reads 100% at 2,047 characters, English but short enough that none of the content dims bite.

So the reader's actual path is: a Filipino hub, describing articles in Filipino, that open as fifteen thousand characters of English, and then a Filipino product on the other side. Nothing is broken - there is NO language toggle on the articles, so no control lies to the reader, and documentElement.lang correctly says "en" on the article and "fil" on the hub, which is what a screen reader needs. The articles load wh-i18n-lite.js and carry three data-i stamps and no page dictionary: the mechanism is present with almost nothing to apply. That is a CONTENT programme, not a code defect, and it stays on Ian's list rather than being papered over with a badge nobody asked for.

INSTRUMENT FAULT 9, FOUND AND FIXED DURING THIS WALK, AND IT CHANGED THESE NUMBERS. B3 decided whether to apply the Flesch-Kincaid grade from window.WH_LANG - the READER'S PREFERENCE - not from the language of the text. So on English-only content read by a Filipino speaker the grade was withheld and the note blamed Filipino calibration. The first survey of the RA 11285 article in this walk reported B3 33% with "grade=n/a"; on the corrected lens the same page, same load, reports B3 0% with grade>8=92 - the exact figure the English walk had recorded. AN ENGLISH PAGE LOOKED BETTER FOR HAVING BEEN READ BY A FILIPINO SPEAKER. The lens now keys on the page's own lang declaration, which read "fil" on all six product pages walked an hour earlier and "en" here; WH_LANG survives only as the fallback for a page that declares no lang at all. Filipino text is still exempt from the grade, which was always right - the learn hub still reports grade=n/a at 99%, correctly, because its text really is Filipino.

THE BLAST RADIUS WAS SIX FINDINGS, AND NARROWING IT WAS THE WHOLE JOB. A retraction keyed on dim B3 + language fil matched SIXTY-NINE banked rows - but on sixty-three of them the page's text really is Filipino and "grade=n/a" is the correct reading, so retracting them would have annotated sixty-three sound findings with a correction that does not apply to them. The rows actually understated were six, all on one article (best-free-cmms-software-philippines), which re-measures at B3 0% with grade>8=15 against the banked grade=n/a. tools/retract_critic_finding.py gained an --ids filter so the correction could be aimed at exactly those six; the replacement finding carries the re-measured number and the reason. A retraction that cannot be narrowed to the rows it is true of is not a correction, it is a second error.

WHAT THIS WALK DID NOT SEE, STATED PLAINLY: this is the DESKTOP half only. The phone-390 half of the same three rows was banked in an earlier session, before the lens correction, so its B3 readings on the two English articles are the old, grade-withheld ones and are a floor rather than the finding. They will correct themselves on the next 390 walk of this path.

The three rows differ only in which hive's data sits behind the same screens; this walk observed Lucena Pharmaceutical Mfg. THE C-AG FIX HOLDS ON A THIRD HIVE, IN ITS HEALTHY PATH. analytics rendered "Karaniwan sa 26 asset" for Manila Electronics Assembly with no raw gateway string anywhere in the page - the walk explicitly checked for "upstream server" and "invalid response was received" and found neither. That is not a test of the failure branch, which still has not been re-observed since the fix and cannot be without inducing a transport failure; it is confirmation that the healthy path is unharmed by the change and that the page names its own hive's asset count correctly.

engineering-design, project-manager AND project-report ARE BYTE-STABLE ACROSS BOTH WIDTHS - 1,889 / 1,771 / 1,482 characters at 390 and at 1280 - which is what a fully responsive layout over identical content looks like. All three carry data-i stamps and almost no _t() calls, so they were candidates for the C-AH class found earlier today; at this persona and this state none of their JS-rendered strings surfaced, which is worth saying plainly: the C-AH census counts 57 literals on project-manager that a different state would show.

TEN READINGS, ALL 100%, AND THE ONLY SUB-100 DIM IS THE DOCUMENTED ONE. analytics N1 75% (label coverage 1/6, data-i=36) at both widths; every other dim on every other page is clean. Fifth Filipino device pair, zero dim delta.

THE WALK'S REAL FIND WAS IN THE SHARED SHELL, AND IT ONLY SHOWED BECAUSE A READ FAILED. report-sender's provenance chip read: "Read failed - Live - contacts refreshed on load, history on load - Batay sa iyong AI reports & report contacts". Four clauses, and the ONLY Filipino words in the sentence are the ones renderSourceChip supplies itself. That function puts `source` through _t() and pushes `freshness`, `window` and `notes` through VERBATIM from 55 call sites across 31 pages - so on every Filipino page this role=status aria-live region is a half-translated sentence, and a screen reader announces it that way.

FIXED WHERE IT BELONGS - ONCE, IN THE SHELL. The freshness clause is the chip's first words and by far the most repeated: 22 distinct literals, of which four cover about thirty of the roughly thirty-eight uses. So it is a phrase map inside renderSourceChip - the same locale-FLOOR pattern utils.js already uses for _t() - rather than 55 site edits. Verified live: logbook now reads "Live - nire-refresh sa pag-load - Batay sa iyong logbook, asset nodes & inventory", alert-hub "Live na data - Batay sa iyong risk scores", dayplanner "Live - nire-refresh sa bawat palit ng view". An unrecognised clause falls through unchanged, so no chip can get worse. HONEST LIMIT, STATED PLAINLY: `window` (11 distinct) and `notes` (43 distinct, one-off explanatory sentences) are STILL ENGLISH and need a per-site copy pass - report-sender's own chip still carries "contacts refreshed on load, history on load" for exactly that reason, and it is visible in this walk's evidence.

TWO MORE FAULTS IN THE SAME FILE, BOTH FOUND BY FOLLOWING THE FIRST. (1) 'Read failed - ' was hard-coded English inserted by the shell into a fil page; now _t('Read failed - ', 'Nabigo ang pagbasa - '), verified by invoking _whSettleStuckLoaders directly rather than waiting for another transport failure. (2) ITS GUARD WAS COUPLED TO AN UNTRANSLATED STRING: it only marked a chip whose text STARTS with "Live", so the day anyone translated that word the honest-degradation marker would have silently stopped appearing and a stale chip would have gone on claiming live data after every read failed. renderSourceChip now stamps data-wh-fresh="1" and that attribute is the primary test, with the text match kept as a fallback. A SAFETY BEHAVIOUR MUST NOT DEPEND ON ANOTHER STRING STAYING IN ENGLISH.

AND THE BRANCH WRITTEN TO HANDLE THE POSSESSIVE LEFT IT IN ENGLISH. dayplanner's chip read "Batay sa your schedule & logbook". renderSourceChip carries a deliberate comment - one whole template per locale, because the possessive sits differently in Filipino - and the branch that detects a leading "your" then glued that English word straight into the Filipino template. Now "Batay sa iyong schedule & logbook", with the English side re-verified unchanged at wh_lang=en ("Based on your schedule & logbook"). A correct intent, documented in a comment, that the code did not carry out.

DAYPLANNER RENDERS FOUR TIMES MORE TEXT AT DESKTOP (4,111 characters against 1,053 at 390) AND NOT ONE DIM MOVES. That is the honest reading of a responsive surface: the phone shows a condensed plan, the desktop the full one, and both are complete for their width. Every other page on this walk is within 140 characters across the two widths.

The three rows differ only in which hive's data sits behind the same screens; this walk observed Baguio Textile Mills. Surveyed: alert-hub 90 dims, 0 sub-100 | analytics 90 dims, 1 sub-100 | dayplanner 90 dims, 0 sub-100 | logbook 90 dims, 0 sub-100 | report-sender 90 dims, 0 sub-100.

THE FIRST ALL-CLEAN WALK OF THE PROGRAM, AND ITS CELL IS THE POINT. Five pages, 450 dims, no finding. That is a real result rather than a shallow one - every survey carries a settle receipt, a fresh lens install and its own viewport - but it should be read for WHICH cell produced it: an English-reading supervisor on a wide screen is the best-supported combination this platform has, and it is the combination most like the people who built it. Set beside the same day's Filipino phone-worker walks, which produced findings on every path, the shape of the platform's real gap is visible: it is strongest for the reader it was written in and thinnest for the worker it was written for.

That contrast is only trustworthy because the ruler was fixed first. Until today four of the rubric's vocabularies read English only - the readability grade, the freshness words, the guidance verbs and the permission wall - and each made the Filipino side look worse than it was. Some of the earlier gap was the instrument. What remains after the correction is the honest difference, and it is smaller than the bank said this morning.

THE FIND IS PLATFORM-WIDE AND IT WAS THE TRANSLATION LAYER ERASING THE PRODUCT'S OWN OUTPUT. founder-console showed a health ring stuck on "Naglo-load..." 75 seconds after load, and still stuck after an explicit Refresh all. It was not a slow fetch and not a permission problem: all 14 panel fetchers settle in 18-1032ms, there are no console errors, and renderHero IS called with real data (overall FAIL, a full summary object) and does not throw. The proof was a three-point sequence on the live element - a sentinel written into it reverted while the page sat idle; the label read "All clear" IMMEDIATELY after render; and it read "Naglo-load..." again 2.5s later. The page computed the right answer every single time and something put the placeholder back.

That something is utils.js's whI18nApply, re-armed by a MutationObserver under FIL (added 2026-09-05 so late-rendered controls get translated - a good change). Its swap loop overwrote the text of EVERY [data-i] element on every re-apply, including elements whose text the application had since computed. #ring-pct-label carries data-i="p_loading_33ce", so each re-apply restored "Loading" over a finished health verdict. Any Filipino page where JS writes into a data-i element had the same wound; founder-console is simply where it was visible enough to catch.

FIXED IN THE SHARED HELPER, and shaped so it does not undo the change it is protecting: the swap now stamps what it wrote (data-i-applied) and, on re-apply, skips any element that no longer holds it - the application owns that text now. A late-rendered node carries no stamp, so it still gets translated, which is the whole reason the observer exists. Verified live: "All clear" survives the debounced re-apply (previously it did not), the ring reads 97%, and 107 static labels on the same page are still translated.

A HYPOTHESIS I HELD AND THE EVIDENCE REFUTED, recorded because the wrong version is the more alarming one. Seeing a fleet supervisor reach the founder console with every value blank, I first read it as the refused-read trap - RLS filtering to nothing and the UI calling it "loading" instead of "not yours". Two checks killed that. Probing the founder RPCs with ROSA'S OWN session (never an owner connection) returned 0, 0 and [] with no error and no other hive's data, so the boundary holds and nothing leaks. And the page does have an honest wall - #no-access-gate, which my first probe missed only because it scans for .gate-card / [id^=gate-] and this one is named differently. She reached the console because IS_LOCAL_FOUNDER is a deliberate localhost bypass. There is no access defect here; the defect was the i18n clobber, and it is a better find than the one I guessed.

Surveyed: analytics 90 dims, 1 sub-100 | community 90 dims, 0 sub-100 | hive 90 dims, 1 sub-100 | ph-intelligence 90 dims, 0 sub-100. [2026-09-11] RETRACTED (interpretation only - the measurement stands): C1 - "hive: C1 67% - bigSizes=[32,24,22] distinct=11". C-AL'S MECHANISM WAS WRONG AND IS WITHDRAWN. This walk reported that hive renders a FOURTH display tier (26px) only at desktop, making C1 33% + A1 75% a width phenomenon, and said so against a baseline of four flat Filipino device pairs. The NUMBERS stand - at 390 the page read C1 67% with bigSizes=[32,24,22]; at 1280 it read C1 33% with bigSizes=[32,26,24,22] and A1 75%, minutes apart on one lens - but the CAUSE is not width. Re-measured the same day, same persona, same page, at DESKTOP in both languages: bigSizes=[32,24,22,21], NO 26px tier, and hive reads 100%. Desktop without the fourth tier refutes "desktop renders the fourth tier" on its own. The 26px tier belongs to the "Your hive's value" card - three tiles at font-size:1.6rem (25.6px), ids vs-pms / vs-faults / vs-knowledge. Those tiles are PRESENT and VISIBLE in both readings; what differs is whether they have their NUMBERS yet. C1 counts type tiers among elements that HAVE TEXT, so an unpopulated 25.6px tile is invisible to it and a populated one is a fourth tier. The desktop half caught the card filled (4,830 characters) and the phone half caught it empty (4,022) - a DATA-ARRIVAL difference the walk read as a LAYOUT difference. My settle rule passed both because each was stable in length; stable is not the same as populated, which is the audit-log frozen-skeleton lesson in a second costume. What is retracted is the interpretation, not the measurement: hive's C1/A1 pair fires when the hive-value tiles are populated, and the width axis - like the "Manila only" attribution it was correcting - remains unseparated. Recorded rather than quietly deleted, because the discipline that caught this is the one that produced the wrong claim in the first place: walk the pair back to back, then check that the mechanism reproduces. [2026-09-11] RETRACTED (interpretation only - the measurement stands): C1 - "hive: C1 67% - bigSizes=[32,24,22] distinct=11". C-AL, SECOND CORRECTION - THE TILES ALWAYS HAD THEIR NUMBERS. The first retraction said hive's C1/A1 pair turns on whether the "Your hive's value" tiles have been POPULATED. That is wrong in detail and is corrected here. The tiles ALWAYS have their numbers: #vs-pms reads innerHTML "460", #vs-faults "7,675", #vs-knowledge "1,700" in every reading. What varies is whether they are RENDERED - the card sits inside <details id="health-details" class="wh-disclose">, a CLOSED disclosure, and innerText correctly returns nothing for content inside one while getBoundingClientRect still reports a box (79x28). That combination - a box with no text - is exactly what made the element look "visible but unpopulated" to my probe and invisible to C1, which counts type tiers among elements that HAVE TEXT. So the real trigger is the DISCLOSURE'S OPEN STATE, not data arrival and not width: on fresh loads #health-details is closed at BOTH 390 and 1280, verified in both languages, and hive reads C1 67% with bigSizes=[32,24,22]. The J21 desktop half caught it OPEN, which revealed three 25.6px tiles and made a fourth type tier. THE GENERAL PROPERTY IS WORTH MORE THAN THE FINDING: a page is graded differently depending on whether a disclosure happens to be expanded, because innerText is a RENDERING-dependent API. A survey that does not expand disclosures is measuring the collapsed page, and getBoundingClientRect will not tell it so - the box is there either way. This is the platform's own "expand everything, scroll to the last element" QA rule arriving as a measurement fact. The measurements on these rows stand as readings of the COLLAPSED page; what is withdrawn, twice now, is any claim about WHY they differ from the J21 desktop half.

AND THE COMPARISON FOUND THE NINTH AND TENTH INSTRUMENT FAULTS' SIBLING: THE RULER SCORED THE SAME PAGE HIGHER IN FILIPINO BECAUSE IT COULD NOT READ THE LANGUAGE. marketplace-seller read 96% in English with FOUR findings - G3 0%, J1 0% "1 destructive control(s)", A3 75%, Z3 96% "risk mis-tap: Delete(destructive)" - and 98% in Filipino with only THREE, J1 and Z3 absent. The page is the same page. Its listing delete button is a marked command button, class="btn-sm danger" data-action="delete", 72x44, plainly visible, and it renders "Delete" in English and "Burahin" in Filipino.

BOTH DETECTORS READ ONLY ENGLISH WORDS. J1's filter tested the label against /delete|remove|clear|reset|archive|discard/ and nothing else; Z3's hazard test had the same vocabulary. Under wh_lang=fil the button matched neither, so J1 fell through to N/A "read-only surface: 0 destructive controls" - the phrase that says a page has nothing to lose - on a page with an unguarded delete button, and Z3 reported no mis-tap hazard. A Filipino reader has exactly the same button and exactly the same risk.

THE FIX WAS ALREADY WRITTEN DOWN IN THE FILE'S OWN COMMENTS. Z3's note says a real destructive control is "a command button (data-action=delete, .danger), never a filter". Those markers are language-independent, and Z3 was already testing className - it just had no entry for "danger". Both dims now lead on the structural markers, with the word test kept for unmarked controls and widened to the Filipino imperatives (burahin, alisin, tanggalin). Re-measured: Filipino reads 96% with J1 0% and "Z3 96% ... Burahin(destructive)", identical to English apart from the label quoted in the receipt. ENGLISH RE-VERIFIED UNCHANGED at 96% with the same four dims, so nothing was double-counted.

THE SCOPE WAS CHECKED, NOT ASSUMED, AND THAT CHANGED THE ANSWER BY TWO ORDERS OF MAGNITUDE. 216 banked Filipino rows cover a page whose SOURCE carries such a marker. But a class in the source is not a control on the screen: logbook renders none of them in the state a walk meets, and asset-hub renders none either - it reads J1 N/A and 100%, correctly. The confirmed set is the 18 rows covering marketplace-seller, and of those only the SIX walked today can be verified, because the older twelve recorded "15 controls, 4 primary CTA" against today's 17 - a different page state, whose delete button I cannot retroactively prove was on screen. inventory READS 100% with its CTA "Order 3 low parts ->" and its chip "Live - refreshed on load - Based on your inventory & stock movements", both correct English - the other half of today's C-AH and C-AK fixes, confirming the phrase map and the _t() wrapping return English unchanged.

[2026-09-11] RETRACTED and REMOVED (the measurement itself is false): J1 - "marketplace-seller: J1 0% - 1 destructive control(s)". INSTRUMENT FAULT 11 - J1 CALLED A GUARDED CONTROL UNGUARDED, AND THIS RETRACTION INCLUDES SIX ROWS I BANKED EARLIER TODAY. J1's slipGuarded could not follow EVENT DELEGATION. marketplace-seller's listing delete is <button class="btn-sm danger" data-action="delete">Delete</button>, wired by a delegated listener - `if (btn.dataset.action === 'delete') handleDelete(btn.dataset.id);` - and handleDelete's FIRST acts are svcRequireOnline() and `await window.whConfirm("Delete ...? This cannot be undone.")`. The control was never unguarded. The lens missed it because all three of its routes were closed: the button carries no onclick, it carries no id, and its distinctive class sits inside a TEMPLATE LITERAL 465 lines from the guard, so neither the id nor the class window ever reached handleDelete - and `typeof window[fn]` fails too, because handleDelete is declared inside the page's IIFE and never attached to window. FOUND ON resume.html, WHERE THE SAME BLINDNESS WAS LOUDER: it graded J1 0% - FOURTEEN destructive controls, blocker severity - on a page where every one is guarded, the per-entry remove by `pushUndo(); snapshotVersion('before remove')` under a comment that says "a novice fat-fingers the X - push undo FIRST so the (already-visible) Undo button can restore it", and the resume delete by an inline yes/no. FIXED in the lens: GUARD now knows the camelCase mechanism names this codebase actually uses (pushUndo, showUndo, snapshotVersion), the element's data-* action token is an anchor in its own right, and the hop follows a CALL in that window to the callee's DECLARED BODY. Re-measured: resume J1 0% -> 100% (page 97% -> 98%), and marketplace-seller's delete resolves guarded via handleDelete, verified by replicating the detector against that page's own inline JS. WHAT SURVIVES AND WHAT DOES NOT: fault 10's DETECTION half stands - J1 and Z3 must SEE a delete button whose label reads "Burahin", and before today they did not - but the VERDICT it produced was wrong, so the J1 finding is removed rather than kept. Z3's mis-tap findings are untouched: crowding is about size and spacing, not about whether an undo exists.

J27, A DEAL GOES WRONG, walked in FILIPINO at phone-390: marketplace -> marketplace-seller-profile -> marketplace -> platform-actions -> hive -> audit-log. Hector Salvador, hectorsalvador@auth.workhiveph.com, supervisor of Manila Electronics Assembly acting as the BUYER, wh_lang=fil, walked minutes after the same path in English at desktop.

audit-log READS 100% AT 1,958 CHARACTERS with main-content display:block at the FIRST read and no gate - today's C-AI fix confirmed for a SUPERVISOR in Filipino, on a third route. The whole risk of that fix was that hiding the chrome early for a non-supervisor might strand a supervisor behind a blank page; it does not, in either language.

hive READS 99% WITH C1 67% AND bigSizes=[32,24,22] - the COLLAPSED page, which is what a reader meets on arrival, and the reading that finally explained the C-AL confusion. The "Your hive's value" card lives inside <details id="health-details">, closed by default at BOTH widths in BOTH languages (verified on fresh loads). Its three tiles hold their numbers the whole time - innerHTML reads 460, 7,675 and 1,700 - but innerText returns NOTHING for content inside a closed disclosure while getBoundingClientRect still reports a 79x28 box. A box with no text is not "still loading"; it is NOT RENDERED. C1 counts type tiers among elements that HAVE TEXT, so the 25.6px tiles are invisible while collapsed and are a fourth tier when expanded. That is the whole mechanism, and it is neither width nor data arrival - my first two explanations, both withdrawn.

platform-actions READS 98% and IS RENDERING TWO LANGUAGES UNDER ONE DECLARATION. Its chrome is Filipino - "Paano gumagana ang console na ito", "Balik sa WorkHive", "Hive Board Ko" - while its body is English by design: "Governance actions only: approve/verify/resolve. Every metric (health, usage, growth, marketplace volumes) lives in Grafana." Counted on the visible text: 42 Filipino function-word hits against 39 English. documentElement.lang reads "fil" for all of it, and NO element on the page declares a lang of its own. A screen reader will therefore pronounce the English body with Filipino phonetics - WCAG 3.1.2 Language of Parts. ph-intelligence has the same shape: lang="fil", exactly one element declaring a language (the html element), no translate="no" region, and visibly mixed text.

WHAT I DID NOT DO ABOUT IT, AND WHY. The obvious fix is to mark the EN body region lang="en" so the markup says what these pages' own EN-by-design comments already say. I did not make it: on ph-intelligence the surface a walker can reach is the MATURITY GATE, not the report body, so the region a fix would target was never on screen, and on platform-actions the two languages are interleaved rather than separated into a body wrapper. Fixing what I cannot see is how a plausible edit becomes a wrong one. Recorded for Ian with the measurement attached; it is a real standards finding on three EN-by-design pages, and it needs someone to decide where the language boundary actually is.

B3 READS 67% HERE AND 33% IN ENGLISH ON THE SAME PAGE, and that gap is fault 9's corrected rule doing the conservative thing rather than the right thing: the grade is withheld because documentElement.lang says "fil", even though roughly half the graded sentences are English. Withholding is the safe direction - it never invents a bad score - but it is worth saying plainly that on a genuinely bilingual page the lens now measures less than it could, and the remedy is the same lang-of-parts markup the finding above asks for.

marketplace 100%, marketplace-seller-profile 99% (B3 33%, grade correctly withheld on Filipino text).

The three rows differ only in which hive's data sits behind the same screens; this walk observed Manila Electronics Assembly. Widened with tokens DERIVED by pairing every i18n/pages/*.fil.json entry against the EN string on its own data-i element and keeping the FIL halves whose ENGLISH half the regex already matched: noong (as of), buhay (alive), nabuo (generated, the completed form - only the present-tense binubuo was known). `magagawa` was deliberately left out: its English half is "reports CAN BE generated", a capability claim, and a token that excuses a chip saying nothing about WHEN is worse than a missing one. The English rendering is still a defect and is still reported - as what it is: the app wrote English into a stamped element. Grade the outcome, but describe the mechanism truthfully or the worklist sends someone to the wrong file.

THE BOUNDARY HOLDS AT THE DATA LAYER, NOT ONLY AT THE GATE CARD - AND THE PROOF NEEDED TWO PEOPLE. Asking as the worker, with HIS OWN session and never an owner or service connection, both audit tables returned ZERO rows and NO error - including when explicitly asking for a hive that is not his (.neq('hive_id', mine)). Zero rows is not by itself evidence of anything: it reads identically whether RLS withheld the rows or the table is simply empty, and stopping there would have been a boundary claim resting on an ambiguity. The same query run as Rosa dela Cruz, supervisor of Dela Cruz Delivery Fleet, with HER own session, returns 20 rows of hive_audit_log and 0 rows from any other hive. So the table demonstrably holds rows, the worker's identical unscoped request returned none of them, and the supervisor who may read them sees only her own hive's. Two personas, two tokens, one query - that is what makes it a finding rather than an absence.

Two things follow. The gate card on audit-log is NOT the security boundary, it is the honest EXPLANATION of one that already holds underneath; a UI-only wall would have leaked here and did not. And the refusal is SILENT - 0 rows, no error - which is the fourth state a reader can misread as "there is nothing", so the page showing "Supervisors only" instead of an empty list is doing exactly the right thing. The same walk earlier today confirmed the rubric now scores that wall as N/A rather than three hard zeros.

An honest note on method: my FIRST probe queried a table called `audit_log` and came back PGRST205, "could not find the table in the schema cache". That is not evidence of a boundary - it is evidence of a wrong table name, and reporting it as a clean refusal would have been a false pass. The real names came from the page's own queries (hive_audit_log, ai_audit_log), which is where they should have come from first.

THE MEASUREMENT STANDS AND MY EXPLANATION OF IT WAS WRONG. These findings were banked with the story "the Filipino translation outgrew its English original - the English is under twenty words and the translation is not". The Filipino sentence really is over the limit, so the finding itself is real and stays. But the reason was false, and the correct one is worse: the ENGLISH original is 24 words, also over the limit, and it PASSED only because its source is hard-wrapped in the HTML. B3's sentence splitter treated a newline as a sentence boundary, so public-feed's English hint was chopped into eight fragments by its markup line breaks - including the one-word "sentence" You, and "only, never here, unless you share it." starting mid-clause - longest fragment 17 words, so the dim passed it. The same prose in Filipino arrives from a dictionary as ONE unbroken string, is measured as the sentence it actually is, and fails. So the check was reading how the HTML happens to be wrapped rather than how long the sentences are: it under-reported hard-wrapped English markup and correctly measured anything delivered from JSON or JS. That asymmetry is STRUCTURAL, not a translation problem - English lives in hard-wrapped HTML and Filipino comes from single-line dictionaries - and it is the opposite of what these rows claimed. The ruler is fixed by asking the CSS the question it already answers: if an element PRESERVES whitespace (pre/pre-wrap/pre-line) a newline is a line the reader sees and still splits, and if the element COLLAPSES it the newline is invisible formatting and the text is one flowing run. Verified both ways live - public-feed in English now reads B3 33% with "worst(24w)" named, exposing a long sentence and a grade-over-8 offender that its own markup had been hiding, and shift-brain's [SAFETY] ACTIVE ISOLATIONS pre-wrap list still splits per line and still passes, so the case the newline split existed for is intact. What these rows should say is not "the translation is too long" but "this sentence is too long in BOTH languages, and only the Filipino half was visible".

Cast as bryangarcia@auth.workhiveph.com, a WORKER in Baguio Textile Mills, asking at every step what he can reach that is not his. No adversary had been cast in this program before. Session verified through getDb().auth.getSession(). 1280x860 CSS per survey, each page graded only after its text length held steady across three consecutive reads. 450 dims graded, 5 sub-100.

THE BOUNDARY HOLDS AT THE DATA LAYER, NOT ONLY AT THE GATE CARD - AND THE PROOF NEEDED TWO PEOPLE. Asking as the worker, with HIS OWN session and never an owner or service connection, both audit tables returned ZERO rows and NO error - including when explicitly asking for a hive that is not his (.neq('hive_id', mine)). Zero rows is not by itself evidence of anything: it reads identically whether RLS withheld the rows or the table is simply empty, and stopping there would have been a boundary claim resting on an ambiguity. The same query run as Rosa dela Cruz, supervisor of Dela Cruz Delivery Fleet, with HER own session, returns 20 rows of hive_audit_log and 0 rows from any other hive. So the table demonstrably holds rows, the worker's identical unscoped request returned none of them, and the supervisor who may read them sees only her own hive's. Two personas, two tokens, one query - that is what makes it a finding rather than an absence.

Two things follow. The gate card on audit-log is NOT the security boundary, it is the honest EXPLANATION of one that already holds underneath; a UI-only wall would have leaked here and did not. And the refusal is SILENT - 0 rows, no error - which is the fourth state a reader can misread as "there is nothing", so the page showing "Supervisors only" instead of an empty list is doing exactly the right thing. The same walk earlier today confirmed the rubric now scores that wall as N/A rather than three hard zeros.

An honest note on method: my FIRST probe queried a table called `audit_log` and came back PGRST205, "could not find the table in the schema cache". That is not evidence of a boundary - it is evidence of a wrong table name, and reporting it as a clean refusal would have been a false pass. The real names came from the page's own queries (hive_audit_log, ai_audit_log), which is where they should have come from first.

public-feed and achievements read 100%, with zero i18n orphans on all five pages.

THE MEASUREMENT STANDS AND MY EXPLANATION OF IT WAS WRONG. These findings were banked with the story "the Filipino translation outgrew its English original - the English is under twenty words and the translation is not". The Filipino sentence really is over the limit, so the finding itself is real and stays. But the reason was false, and the correct one is worse: the ENGLISH original is 24 words, also over the limit, and it PASSED only because its source is hard-wrapped in the HTML. B3's sentence splitter treated a newline as a sentence boundary, so public-feed's English hint was chopped into eight fragments by its markup line breaks - including the one-word "sentence" You, and "only, never here, unless you share it." starting mid-clause - longest fragment 17 words, so the dim passed it. The same prose in Filipino arrives from a dictionary as ONE unbroken string, is measured as the sentence it actually is, and fails. So the check was reading how the HTML happens to be wrapped rather than how long the sentences are: it under-reported hard-wrapped English markup and correctly measured anything delivered from JSON or JS. That asymmetry is STRUCTURAL, not a translation problem - English lives in hard-wrapped HTML and Filipino comes from single-line dictionaries - and it is the opposite of what these rows claimed. The ruler is fixed by asking the CSS the question it already answers: if an element PRESERVES whitespace (pre/pre-wrap/pre-line) a newline is a line the reader sees and still splits, and if the element COLLAPSES it the newline is invisible formatting and the text is one flowing run. Verified both ways live - public-feed in English now reads B3 33% with "worst(24w)" named, exposing a long sentence and a grade-over-8 offender that its own markup had been hiding, and shift-brain's [SAFETY] ACTIVE ISOLATIONS pre-wrap list still splits per line and still passes, so the case the newline split existed for is intact. What these rows should say is not "the translation is too long" but "this sentence is too long in BOTH languages, and only the Filipino half was visible".

rows.clean_note:
One in-motion MCP walk, banked onto 7 row(s) that share its cell, page path, language, condition and moment (they differ only in which hive's data sits behind the screens - see tools/critic_walk_groups.py). J1 ONBOARDING, walked step by step through chrome-devtools-mcp: index -> hive -> asset-hub -> logbook -> pm-scheduler -> alert-hub, phone-390 mobile+touch, English, normal conditions, present moment. Walked the way a new user actually arrives: index SIGNED OUT (the front door, no session at all), then in through the platform's own wall, then the member surfaces as Rosa dela Cruz of Dela Cruz Delivery Fleet - the sparsest seeded hive (0 FMEA modes, 0 strategies, an empty day plan), which is the closest thing the fixtures have to a hive that has just started. index 252,114 chars signed-out; hive 406,741, logbook 370,249, asset-hub 270,424, pm-scheduler 187,120, alert-hub 155,111 signed in. Every survey taken after a navigation and carrying install:true - a fresh lens per page, proven, not assumed. 540 dims graded.

THE FRONT DOOR IS THE WEAKEST SURFACE THIS PROGRAM HAS WALKED, AND MOST OF WHAT MADE IT LOOK WEAK WAS THE RULER. index first graded 81% with 14 sub-100 dims, against 98-100% on every signed-in page in the same walk. Six of those dims turned out to share ONE cause, and it was not the page: index ships a <section class="sr-only"> text sitemap - a screen-reader link list hidden with the standard clip pattern (1x1 box, overflow:hidden, clip:rect(0,0,0,0)). `clip` hides PAINT, not LAYOUT, so the 32 links inside keep their natural rects: they measured 1365x22, 1486x22, 1960x22 - wider than the 390px viewport, at x=-1, 22px tall - and checkVisibility() calls them visible because they are not display:none, not visibility:hidden and not opacity:0. The lens was reading 32 unpaintable links as real page content on the platform's front door: F1 46% and K2 50% (undersized tap targets nobody can tap), Z3 55% (crowded targets), G3 counting 59 "controls" against 27 real ones, G2 0% (the sitemap's own "Marketplace: Buyer-facing ..." line read as leaked system jargon in the page's copy) and B3 running a 104-"sentence" prose census against 19 real ones.

FIXED IN THE SHARED VISIBILITY PREDICATE, not in any one dim: an ancestor collapsed to <=1px in either axis while clipping its overflow is the clip pattern by construction, whatever it is called (.sr-only, .visually-hidden, a bespoke rule). R1 already guarded its own slice of this ("a root-level child is never legitimately <=1px"); the rule now lives where every dim inherits it, and Z3 - which collects its own targets through _vz - calls the same helper. Re-measured: index 81% -> 88%, sub-100 14 -> 9, F1 100% ("all >= 44px"), K2 100% ("0 under-44 target(s)"), Z3 clear, G2 clear, B3's census 104 -> 19 sentences, G3's control count 59 -> 27 - with the 32 sr-only links STILL IN THE DOM. The page was never changed; only the ruler was.

A SECOND INSTRUMENT CORRECTION, AND THE PRODUCT HARDENED BESIDE IT. index also graded Q2 0% - "10 focusable control(s) are opacity:0 yet still in the tab order (keyboard lands on an invisible control)". The controls are real links inside scroll-reveal sections, so the snapshot was accurate, but Q2's claim is BEHAVIOURAL and a snapshot cannot settle it. Tested on a clean load: focusing one scrolls it into view, the IntersectionObserver fires, .visible lands - opacity 0 -> 0.92 at 300ms -> 1 at 700ms. No keyboard user lands on anything that stays invisible. (An earlier probe said the opposite and was the unreliable one - it ran on a page where the rubric had already been installed and surveyed. Re-run on a fresh load, it reversed.) So index.html now DECLARES the guarantee rather than leaving it emergent - `.reveal:focus-within { opacity: 1 }` makes the section visible the instant focus enters it, with no dependence on the observer firing, the scroll happening or the 0.12 threshold being met - and Q2 now reads that declaration, scanning same-origin stylesheets for a rule that restores opacity on :focus-within. An ancestor with no such rule still fails, which is the case the dim exists for. Re-measured: Q2 100%, "71 focusable control(s), none hidden-but-focusable".

ONE PRODUCT FIX ON THE MEMBER SIDE: pm-scheduler's "No Data" status badge coloured its text #9ca3af (grey-400), measuring 4.13:1 at 0.65rem uppercase against the 4.5:1 small text owes. There is no --wh-grey-text token, but the platform had already tuned this exact semantic once - renderKpiTile's "No data" row was raised to rgba(255,255,255,0.78) on 2026-09-07 after a 24px APCA reading (Lc 0/45) showed WCAG waving through what APCA would not. Reused that value rather than inventing a second opinion for one meaning. pm-scheduler re-read C2 with ZERO offenders and 100% overall.

THE THIRTEEN FINDINGS BANKED are what survived all of that, and they concentrate on the front door: index still carries 9 (B2/B1 marketese "SMRP world-class benchmarks", E3 no source chip, G3 3 primary CTAs, O2 no on-demand help, T1 one overflow:hidden box clipping content below the fold at 390px, B3 reading grade, A3 no disclosures, N1 label coverage 2/3), against hive 2 (G3, A3), asset-hub 1 (B3 passive voice), alert-hub 1 (R3 card treatments) and logbook and pm-scheduler clean at 100%. That shape is worth stating plainly: the signed-in product this persona reaches is in good order, and the page a NEW user meets first is where the remaining work is. Surveyed: alert-hub 90 dims, 1 sub-100 | asset-hub 90 dims, 1 sub-100 | hive 90 dims, 2 sub-100 | index 90 dims, 9 sub-100 | logbook 90 dims, 0 sub-100 | pm-scheduler 90 dims, 0 sub-100. [2026-09-11] RETRACTED and REMOVED (the measurement itself is false): T1 - "index: T1 0% - 1 overflow:hidden box(es) clip content below the fold @390 (unreachable)". The lens was wrong, not the page. T1's scrollHeight test says only that SOMETHING overflows an overflow:hidden box; it cannot say WHAT, and the finding then asserted 'content below the fold (unreachable)'. Measured on index at 390: the hero (relative max-w-7xl ... py-24 lg:py-32 overflow-hidden) clips 52px, and the SOLE overhanging element is a decorative gradient - div.absolute.inset-0.rounded-3xl.opacity-30 with pointer-events:none, 999px tall, overhanging by 51px, carrying no text, no link and no button. The overflow:hidden is doing exactly its job: containing a flourish so it does not bleed past a rounded corner. The old guard already tried to exclude decoration with 'if (pointerEvents === none) continue' but applied that test to the CONTAINER, which has normal pointer-events, while the decoration is the CHILD - the check asked the right question of the wrong element, the same shape as the seven instrument faults before it. T1 now counts a box only when something CONTENT-BEARING is clipped: a descendant that overhangs the box bottom and either carries its own text or is/contains an interactive control, and is not itself pointer-events:none. Re-surveyed live: T1 100 percent, 'no trapped content @390', index 88 to 90 percent. All eleven T1 findings the registry held were this one page and this one false positive; a real scroll-trap still fails the dim.

RETURNER on DESKTOP-1280: index -> hive -> logbook -> audit-log, English, normal conditions, present moment, viewport 1280x900 with mobile/touch emulation OFF, as Rosa dela Cruz, supervisor of Dela Cruz Delivery Fleet. The distinction from the new-user walk banked in the same session is the auth state at the FRONT DOOR: a returner arrives WITH a session, so index was walked signed-in rather than signed-out. Every survey taken after a navigation with install:true. 360 dims graded, 2 sub-100.

THE FRONT DOOR IS A DIFFERENT PAGE FOR A RETURNER, AND IT IS THE STRONGER ONE. index reads 100% here against 91% for the same file walked signed-out at the same viewport in the same session - not a softer grade, a different screen. Signed in it opens "Good afternoon, Rosa", names her hive as a chip that links straight to the board, repeats the route as a "Hive Board" link, and puts three ACTIONABLE items above the fold, each deep-linked to where the work is: "TODAY - AMC BRIEF AWAITING APPROVAL" to alert-hub#amc-card, "2 PM OVERDUE (2 OF 3 ASSETS)" to pm-scheduler?filter=overdue, and "4 PARTS (2 OUT - 2 LOW)" to inventory?status=below. A returner is not shown the marketing page; they are shown their day. That is the answer to the question this persona exists to ask, and it is worth banking as an observed STRENGTH rather than only counting the two defects.

A PROBE ERROR WORTH RECORDING, because it nearly became a finding. An ad-hoc check for "does the front door offer a way back into the hive" returned FALSE - and it was my regex, not the page: it looked for "my hive / back to hive / open hive / hive live board / go to hive" and the page says "Hive Board" and shows the hive by NAME. The page had two routes to hive.html above the fold the whole time. Same shape as the other instrument errors this session: the ad-hoc probe is an oracle too, and it gets checked against the element before its answer is believed.

audit-log reads 100% for this supervisor with both gate cards present and NOT visible - the other side of the permission-wall exemption added earlier in the session, confirming it fires only where the wall actually paints. logbook holds at 100% on desktop after this session's contrast work.

THE TWO FINDINGS BANKED are hive G3 0% (24 controls, 3 primary CTAs against a threshold of 2) and A3 75% (7 disclosures, 10 blocks, primaryCta 3/2). This is the FOURTH walk in the session to land the same pair on hive - phone-390 new-user, desktop-1280 new-user, desktop-1280 growth loop and now the returner - across two viewports and two personas. That consistency is itself the finding: it is not a device or persona artifact, it is the board's own hierarchy, and it is a design decision (which of the three primary CTAs steps down) rather than something to resolve by deleting a control. Left banked with its reasoning, deliberately unfixed. Surveyed: audit-log 90 dims, 0 sub-100 | hive 90 dims, 2 sub-100 | index 90 dims, 0 sub-100 | logbook 90 dims, 0 sub-100.

The rubric's C2 now skips elements inside [disabled] / [aria-disabled=true] / fieldset[disabled], verified in both directions: analytics-report goes 95% -> 100% with its offender list emptied, while logbook's genuine 4.09:1 on 'Instrumentation' still fails at 92%. WHAT REMAINS after that correction: dayplanner, pm-scheduler and analytics-report are clean at 90/90; logbook keeps the one real contrast miss; and report-sender carries three - J1 0% for a single unguarded destructive control on the surface whose whole job is sending a report outward, K2 with one tap target under 44px, and F1 95%. [2026-09-10] RETRACTED and REMOVED (the measurement itself is false): J1 - "report-sender: J1 0% - 1 destructive control(s)". The claim was that report-sender ships an UNGUARDED destructive control, and the severity scale turned the 0% into a BLOCKER. It is false, and the control was never unguarded. The Remove button on a saved recipient chip calls deleteContact(), which opens window.whConfirm() before touching anything and refuses outright when offline. The lens could not see it because BOTH of its routes were closed: the button carries no onclick attribute (it is addEventListener-wired) and no id (it is a template-rendered row keyed by data-del), so the id-anchored source scan never ran. The dim's own comment says a slip-guard is "a MECHANISM, not an attribute spelling", and anchoring on the ID was that same error one level up. J1 now also anchors on a DISTINCTIVE class (>=6 chars and <=8 occurrences, so a generic token like "btn" can never qualify) and follows the handler ONE HOP: the code beside the anchor calls deleteContact(...), and that function's own source carries the guard. The hop window is deliberately tighter than the direct-text window (-60/+300 vs -300/+800), calibrated against a false pass the wide window produced - it let the CONTAINER class contact-chip inherit the guard of the delete wiring rendered a few lines away, which would have excused a control that merely sits near a guarded one. Re-surveyed live on the same page as the same persona: report-sender J1 reads MEASURED 100%, and the page reads 100% overall. Separately and genuinely, that same button was 28x28 and is now 44x44, so the walk's F1/K2 findings on it were real and are fixed.

CORRECTION (2026-09-10, same session): an earlier version of this note read analytics' N1 75% as 'a Filipino-speaking technician meets a page that is largely still English'. That is FALSE and the retraction belongs on the row. N1's label coverage counts `data-i`, the STATIC swapper's marker; the five uncovered labels are the whole uncovered sample and are the 'Show all N assets' expand controls, built at analytics.html:2855 through the platform's OTHER bilingual mechanism, _t(en, fil). Switching the page to FIL renders them 'Ipakita lahat ng 30 asset', 'Ipakita lahat ng 85 pares', 'Ipakita lahat ng 24 piyesa' - they are fully translated. N1 is a MECHANISM census, which its own honest-limit note in survey_ufai_rubric.js says plainly, and reading it as what a reader SEES is the error. The dim now names this blind spot at the measurement itself. [2026-09-11] RETRACTED (interpretation only - the measurement stands): R3 - "analytics: R3 67% - cardTreatments=1 · silhouettes=4 for 3 role(s) (pill,8px,bar,0px)". The NUMBER is right and the STORY told about it was wrong. Every note carrying this finding explained it as the four .phase-tab controls falling back to their own 0px corner once the strip wraps at 390. They do not: the parent still has gap:0 and the tabs still have border-radius:0, so R3's joined-group test reads them as ONE BAR at both widths - they were never the fourth silhouette. Re-measured by replicating R3's own roleOf/shapeV against the page root at 390: pill->select(20), 8px->press(12), bar->navigate(4), 0px->press(6). The fourth silhouette is the six .kpi-toggle expanders - Availability, MTBF, MTTR, PM Compliance Rate, Downtime Pareto, Failure Frequency - wearing a square corner while the page's twelve other press controls (refresh-btn, details-toggle, showall-toggle) wear 8px. It is NOT a responsive defect: the toggle is 308px inside a 352px card (87.5%), just under isCardAnatomy's 90% cut-off, and at desktop it crosses that line and is excluded, which is the only reason R3 read 100% at 1280. The inconsistency existed at every width; one width could see it. Fixed by giving .kpi-toggle var(--wh-radius-sm) - the border and tint come from a JS-written inline style that sets no radius, so the class rule wins. Verified at BOTH widths: pill/8px/bar, 3 shapes for 3 roles, 0 collisions, R3 100%, analytics 100%. A mechanism must be measured, not inferred from the one thing that visibly changed.

A DEAD END FOUND AND FIXED THIS WALK: shift-brain graded X1 at 50% with TWO states where a person landing there had no next step - 'No assets above risk threshold this window' and 'No carry-forward items from the prior shift'. Both are GOOD news and both were a closed room: a supervisor opening the shift planner on a quiet morning was shown an empty page with nowhere to go. Rewritten in the platform's own house style for a zero-state, which already does this well elsewhere ('No recent traces. New AI questions appear here as they run.') - the sentences now lead with what the absence MEANS and then name where to look: 'nothing needs attention. Open Asset Hub to review the full fleet' and 'it closed clean. Open the logbook to see what was done', both translated. Verified live: X1 50 -> 100, 'all 4 conditional state(s) offer a CTA or recovery guidance', taking shift-brain from three sub-100 dims to two. AND THE DEAD ENDS WERE THE SUPERVISOR'S ALONE: walked as a WORKER minutes earlier, the same page at the same viewport passed X1 outright, because those two strips do not render for them. AND THE SAME IS TRUE OF hive.html - it fails G3 (25 controls against 3 primary CTAs), A3 and X1 for this supervisor, and a completely different pair, A2 and N1, for the worker. One page, one screen size, two people, two critiques; a page-at-rest board reports one and cannot say which. The rest: dayplanner H1 with no progress indicator, analytics keeping N1 75% Filipino coverage, R3 67%, B3 67% passive voice and a real 4.18:1 contrast miss. Surveyed: analytics 90 dims, 4 sub-100 | community 90 dims, 0 sub-100 | dayplanner 90 dims, 1 sub-100 | hive 90 dims, 3 sub-100 | ph-intelligence 90 dims, 0 sub-100 | shift-brain 90 dims, 2 sub-100. CORRECTION (2026-09-10, same session): an earlier version of this note read analytics' N1 75% as 'a Filipino-speaking technician meets a page that is largely still English'. That is FALSE and the retraction belongs on the row. N1's label coverage counts `data-i`, the STATIC swapper's marker; the five uncovered labels are the whole uncovered sample and are the 'Show all N assets' expand controls, built at analytics.html:2855 through the platform's OTHER bilingual mechanism, _t(en, fil). Switching the page to FIL renders them 'Ipakita lahat ng 30 asset', 'Ipakita lahat ng 85 pares', 'Ipakita lahat ng 24 piyesa' - they are fully translated. N1 is a MECHANISM census, which its own honest-limit note in survey_ufai_rubric.js says plainly, and reading it as what a reader SEES is the error. The dim now names this blind spot at the measurement itself. [2026-09-10] RETRACTED and REMOVED (the measurement itself is false): X1 - "hive: X1 80% - 1 dead-end state(s) — a user landing there has NO next step: "Nothing to approve on this board."". Re-walked as Rosa dela Cruz (supervisor, Dela Cruz Delivery Fleet) on 2026-09-10 through chrome-devtools-mcp, signed in at the platform's own wall, and re-surveyed with the corrected ruler: hive reads X1 100% (5 of 5). The panel was never a dead end. "Nothing to approve on this board." renders ONLY on the branch where work is waiting elsewhere, and that same branch fills the immediately adjacent #approval-list with the pointer to it, so the person sees one region: the pointer, then the message. X1 scoped the dead-end test to the panel's own subtree, which measured the MARKUP's shape rather than the screen. The ruler now exempts a panel whose immediately adjacent sibling is visible, is not itself an empty-state panel, is not chrome or nav, and carries a control that points somewhere (survey_ufai_rubric.js); the exemption is narrow by construction, because in the ordinary case that sibling list is EMPTY when the message shows and so the panel still reddens. NOT folded into the healthy-zero exemption: "nothing to approve HERE" is not inbox-zero, there IS work, and a page that named nowhere to find it would still be a dead end. THE SAME WALK FOUND A REAL DEFECT IN THAT EXACT REGION, now fixed and verified live: the pointer read "Also awaiting your review in Asset Hub: 2 shift briefings in Alert Hub" while Asset Hub owed this supervisor nothing (0 FMEA modes, 0 strategies) - the Asset Hub clause was unconditional on its own counts, so it named a page with nothing on it and buried the page that did. All three fleet hives sit in exactly that state (Dela Cruz, Ramos, Tan, each 0/0/2), so every fleet supervisor on the platform met it. hive.html now names a destination only when it holds something: verified live as "Also awaiting your review: 2 shift briefings in Alert Hub" for the fleet, and "Also awaiting your review in Asset Hub: 19 FMEA modes - 9 strategies - 2 shift briefings in Alert Hub" for Manila Electronics (19/9/2). So X1 pointed at the right region for the wrong reason: the dead-end claim is withdrawn, and the defect that region actually had is fixed. [2026-09-10] RETRACTED and REMOVED (the measurement itself is false): H1 - "dayplanner: H1 0% - 0 progress indicator(s)". The claim was that dayplanner shows NO progress indicator, and the severity scale turned the 0% into a BLOCKER. It is false, and it inverted the dim's own principle. The page SHIPS the goal-gradient: it renders utils.js's shared whProgressStrip into <div id="dp-progress" class="wh-progress-slot">, and that helper deliberately returns nothing when total is 0 - for exactly the reason H1's own comment gives three lines above the check, that an empty bar invents a journey which does not exist (the A3 decoration error). The walk was cast as a fleet supervisor whose day was genuinely empty ("Nothing scheduled", "No plan yet", 0 open items from Logbook), so the page correctly declined to paint a bar and the dim scored it a blocker for obeying the dim. Confirmed by reading the page rather than the number: dayplanner.html contains no progress markup only because none was rendered in that data state - the two 'bar-track' matches in the file are ::-webkit-scrollbar-track, and the slot itself was present and empty. H1 now reads an EMPTY .wh-progress-slot as the page's own declaration that the mechanism is present with nothing to gradient, and reports N/A with that reason; a worker-daily page with no slot AND no bar still reads 0%, which is the real gap the dim exists to catch. Verified precise in the same session on the same live pages: dayplanner N/A and 100% overall, while logbook (2 indicators) and analytics (8) stay MEASURED at 100% and alert-hub keeps its original not-worker-daily N/A. Stated limit, recorded rather than hidden: the lens cannot distinguish "no data" from "the render broke", so an empty slot yields N/A - not gradable in this state - never a 100% that would claim a bar painted. [2026-09-11] RETRACTED (interpretation only - the measurement stands): R3 - "analytics: R3 67% - cardTreatments=1 · silhouettes=4 for 3 role(s) (pill,8px,bar,0px)". The NUMBER is right and the STORY told about it was wrong. Every note carrying this finding explained it as the four .phase-tab controls falling back to their own 0px corner once the strip wraps at 390. They do not: the parent still has gap:0 and the tabs still have border-radius:0, so R3's joined-group test reads them as ONE BAR at both widths - they were never the fourth silhouette. Re-measured by replicating R3's own roleOf/shapeV against the page root at 390: pill->select(20), 8px->press(12), bar->navigate(4), 0px->press(6). The fourth silhouette is the six .kpi-toggle expanders - Availability, MTBF, MTTR, PM Compliance Rate, Downtime Pareto, Failure Frequency - wearing a square corner while the page's twelve other press controls (refresh-btn, details-toggle, showall-toggle) wear 8px. It is NOT a responsive defect: the toggle is 308px inside a 352px card (87.5%), just under isCardAnatomy's 90% cut-off, and at desktop it crosses that line and is excluded, which is the only reason R3 read 100% at 1280. The inconsistency existed at every width; one width could see it. Fixed by giving .kpi-toggle var(--wh-radius-sm) - the border and tint come from a JS-written inline style that sets no radius, so the class rule wins. Verified at BOTH widths: pill/8px/bar, 3 shapes for 3 roles, 0 collisions, R3 100%, analytics 100%. A mechanism must be measured, not inferred from the one thing that visibly changed.

The NUMBER is right and the STORY told about it was wrong. Every note carrying this finding explained it as the four .phase-tab controls falling back to their own 0px corner once the strip wraps at 390. They do not: the parent still has gap:0 and the tabs still have border-radius:0, so R3's joined-group test reads them as ONE BAR at both widths - they were never the fourth silhouette. Re-measured by replicating R3's own roleOf/shapeV against the page root at 390: pill->select(20), 8px->press(12), bar->navigate(4), 0px->press(6). It is NOT a responsive defect: the toggle is 308px inside a 352px card (87.5%), just under isCardAnatomy's 90% cut-off, and at desktop it crosses that line and is excluded, which is the only reason R3 read 100% at 1280. The inconsistency existed at every width; one width could see it. Fixed by giving .kpi-toggle var(--wh-radius-sm) - the border and tint come from a JS-written inline style that sets no radius, so the class rule wins. Verified at BOTH widths: pill/8px/bar, 3 shapes for 3 roles, 0 collisions, R3 100%, analytics 100%. A mechanism must be measured, not inferred from the one thing that visibly changed.

CORRECTION (2026-09-10, same session): an earlier version of this note read analytics' N1 75% as 'a Filipino-speaking technician meets a page that is largely still English'. That is FALSE and the retraction belongs on the row. N1's label coverage counts `data-i`, the STATIC swapper's marker; the five uncovered labels are the whole uncovered sample and are the 'Show all N assets' expand controls, built at analytics.html:2855 through the platform's OTHER bilingual mechanism, _t(en, fil). Switching the page to FIL renders them 'Ipakita lahat ng 30 asset', 'Ipakita lahat ng 85 pares', 'Ipakita lahat ng 24 piyesa' - they are fully translated. N1 is a MECHANISM census, which its own honest-limit note in survey_ufai_rubric.js says plainly, and reading it as what a reader SEES is the error. The dim now names this blind spot at the measurement itself. [2026-09-11] RETRACTED (interpretation only - the measurement stands): R3 - "analytics: R3 67% - cardTreatments=1 · silhouettes=4 for 3 role(s) (pill,8px,bar,0px)". The NUMBER is right and the STORY told about it was wrong. Every note carrying this finding explained it as the four .phase-tab controls falling back to their own 0px corner once the strip wraps at 390. They do not: the parent still has gap:0 and the tabs still have border-radius:0, so R3's joined-group test reads them as ONE BAR at both widths - they were never the fourth silhouette. Re-measured by replicating R3's own roleOf/shapeV against the page root at 390: pill->select(20), 8px->press(12), bar->navigate(4), 0px->press(6). The fourth silhouette is the six .kpi-toggle expanders - Availability, MTBF, MTTR, PM Compliance Rate, Downtime Pareto, Failure Frequency - wearing a square corner while the page's twelve other press controls (refresh-btn, details-toggle, showall-toggle) wear 8px. It is NOT a responsive defect: the toggle is 308px inside a 352px card (87.5%), just under isCardAnatomy's 90% cut-off, and at desktop it crosses that line and is excluded, which is the only reason R3 read 100% at 1280. The inconsistency existed at every width; one width could see it. Fixed by giving .kpi-toggle var(--wh-radius-sm) - the border and tint come from a JS-written inline style that sets no radius, so the class rule wins. Verified at BOTH widths: pill/8px/bar, 3 shapes for 3 roles, 0 collisions, R3 100%, analytics 100%. A mechanism must be measured, not inferred from the one thing that visibly changed.

J-fleet supervisor operate: alert-hub -> logbook -> dayplanner -> analytics, phone-390 mobile+touch, English, normal conditions, present moment, walked as Rosa dela Cruz, supervisor of Dela Cruz Delivery Fleet, signed in through the platform's OWN wall (her username is "delacruzfleet", the local part of her account, not her display name). Identity survived every hop and every surface rendered: alert-hub 155,264 chars, logbook 369,155, dayplanner 150,311, analytics 150,332. 360 dims graded across the four surfaces, 5 sub-100.

WHAT THE WALK SAW THAT A BOARD AT REST CANNOT. logbook grades a clean 100/90-dims for this persona, and the C2 4.09:1 "Instrumentation" contrast finding banked from the Manila Electronics worker walk does NOT appear here - that string is an asset name in another hive's data, so the same file scores differently for a fleet supervisor. A page's score is a claim about ONE persona in ONE auth state, and this pair of walks is the evidence.

AN INSTRUMENT ERROR THIS WALK FOUND AND FIXED, before banking anything. dayplanner first graded H1 0% - "0 progress indicator(s)" - which the severity scale turns into a BLOCKER. It was false. The page ships the goal-gradient: it renders utils.js's shared whProgressStrip into <div id="dp-progress" class="wh-progress-slot">, and that helper deliberately returns nothing when total is 0, for the reason H1's own comment gives - an empty bar invents a journey that does not exist. Rosa's day was genuinely empty ("Nothing scheduled", "No plan yet", 0 open items), so the page correctly declined to paint a bar, and the dim scored it a blocker for obeying the dim. H1 now reads an EMPTY .wh-progress-slot as the page's own declaration that the mechanism is present with nothing to gradient, and reports N/A with that reason; a worker-daily page with no slot AND no bar still reads 0%, which is the real gap the dim exists to catch. Verified precise in the same session: dayplanner N/A, while logbook (2 indicators) and analytics (8) stay MEASURED at 100%, and alert-hub keeps its original not-worker-daily N/A. Stated limit: the lens cannot tell "no data" from "the render broke", so the empty slot yields N/A - not gradable in this state - never a 100% that would claim a bar painted.

THE FIVE FINDINGS BANKED are all genuine measurements re-read after that correction: alert-hub and analytics both R3 67% (one card treatment against four silhouettes for three roles), analytics B3 67% (2 passive sentences of 27), analytics N1 75% (data-i label coverage 1 of 2), analytics C2 98% (worst 4.18:1 on the "Critical" chip - verified earlier today against WCAG's disabled-control exemption and still a genuine fail on an active control). Surveyed: alert-hub 90 dims, 1 sub-100 | analytics 90 dims, 4 sub-100 | dayplanner 90 dims, 0 sub-100 | logbook 90 dims, 0 sub-100. [2026-09-11] RETRACTED (interpretation only - the measurement stands): R3 - "analytics: R3 67% - cardTreatments=1 · silhouettes=4 for 3 role(s) (pill,8px,bar,0px)". The NUMBER is right and the STORY told about it was wrong. Every note carrying this finding explained it as the four .phase-tab controls falling back to their own 0px corner once the strip wraps at 390. They do not: the parent still has gap:0 and the tabs still have border-radius:0, so R3's joined-group test reads them as ONE BAR at both widths - they were never the fourth silhouette. Re-measured by replicating R3's own roleOf/shapeV against the page root at 390: pill->select(20), 8px->press(12), bar->navigate(4), 0px->press(6). The fourth silhouette is the six .kpi-toggle expanders - Availability, MTBF, MTTR, PM Compliance Rate, Downtime Pareto, Failure Frequency - wearing a square corner while the page's twelve other press controls (refresh-btn, details-toggle, showall-toggle) wear 8px. It is NOT a responsive defect: the toggle is 308px inside a 352px card (87.5%), just under isCardAnatomy's 90% cut-off, and at desktop it crosses that line and is excluded, which is the only reason R3 read 100% at 1280. The inconsistency existed at every width; one width could see it. Fixed by giving .kpi-toggle var(--wh-radius-sm) - the border and tint come from a JS-written inline style that sets no radius, so the class rule wins. Verified at BOTH widths: pill/8px/bar, 3 shapes for 3 roles, 0 collisions, R3 100%, analytics 100%. A mechanism must be measured, not inferred from the one thing that visibly changed.

THE WALK FOUND A SENTENCE THAT NAMED THE WRONG GAP, AND IT ONLY APPEARS IN A HIVE THAT LACKS ONE PARTICULAR HALF OF ITS DATA. analytics read B3 67% on passive=2 - "Performance dimension will activate when planned production rate is configured." twice under a blank OEE tile. So the half that blocks OEE here is QUALITY - and the card was telling a fleet supervisor to configure a planned production rate, which is the PERFORMANCE input. Following the only instruction on screen would have changed nothing.

[2026-09-11] RETRACTED (interpretation only - the measurement stands): R3 - "analytics: R3 67% - cardTreatments=1 · silhouettes=4 for 3 role(s) (pill,8px,bar,0px)". The NUMBER is right and the STORY told about it was wrong. Every note carrying this finding explained it as the four .phase-tab controls falling back to their own 0px corner once the strip wraps at 390. They do not: the parent still has gap:0 and the tabs still have border-radius:0, so R3's joined-group test reads them as ONE BAR at both widths - they were never the fourth silhouette. Re-measured by replicating R3's own roleOf/shapeV against the page root at 390: pill->select(20), 8px->press(12), bar->navigate(4), 0px->press(6). The fourth silhouette is the six .kpi-toggle expanders - Availability, MTBF, MTTR, PM Compliance Rate, Downtime Pareto, Failure Frequency - wearing a square corner while the page's twelve other press controls (refresh-btn, details-toggle, showall-toggle) wear 8px. It is NOT a responsive defect: the toggle is 308px inside a 352px card (87.5%), just under isCardAnatomy's 90% cut-off, and at desktop it crosses that line and is excluded, which is the only reason R3 read 100% at 1280. The inconsistency existed at every width; one width could see it. Fixed by giving .kpi-toggle var(--wh-radius-sm) - the border and tint come from a JS-written inline style that sets no radius, so the class rule wins. Verified at BOTH widths: pill/8px/bar, 3 shapes for 3 roles, 0 collisions, R3 100%, analytics 100%. A mechanism must be measured, not inferred from the one thing that visibly changed.

The same six screens the machine-fed and shift rounds walked, met in the order a person chooses rather than the order a sensor forces, and the readings agree with those rounds page for page. That agreement is the point of the third ordering: it separates what a page IS from what the walker happened to arrive from.

That tells the AI where to look first." - now holds on an English desktop, a Filipino desktop, an English phone as a worker on two different entry orders, and here as the walk's FIRST page rather than its third. Entering cold on the rewritten copy is the harder test and it passes.

analytics REPEATS C-J AT PHONE WIDTH ON A FOURTH PATH: R3 67%, cardTreatments=1 with four control silhouettes (pill, 8px, bar, 0px) for three roles. The mechanism is documented - the four .phase-tab controls sit contiguous at 1280 and wrap into a 2x2 grid at 390, so their square bar-segment corners read as four detached rectangles. Its N1 75% rides alongside (label coverage 1/6, data-i=36) in ENGLISH, which is again the plain evidence that N1 is not a Filipino artifact.

hive REPEATS ITS WORKER-SIDE PAIR ON A SEVENTH CAST: A2 50% with headings=1 across 9 blocks - a worker in the quiet Baguio hive gets nine blocks under the hive's name and nothing between them - and N1 75% in ENGLISH. And again the G3/A3 CTA-competition pair does NOT appear. It has now been absent on every worker cast and present on every supervisor one, which is the observation that scoped that cluster to the supervisor's board rather than to the page.

audit-log IS THE WORKER'S LOCKED CARD, gate visible, 391 characters, 40 of 90 dims correctly N/A. Surveyed: analytics 90 dims, 2 sub-100 | asset-hub 90 dims, 0 sub-100 | audit-log 90 dims, 2 sub-100 | hive 90 dims, 2 sub-100 | logbook 90 dims, 0 sub-100 | pm-scheduler 90 dims, 0 sub-100. [2026-09-11] RETRACTED (interpretation only - the measurement stands): R3 - "analytics: R3 67% - cardTreatments=1 · silhouettes=4 for 3 role(s) (pill,8px,bar,0px)". The NUMBER is right and the STORY told about it was wrong. Every note carrying this finding explained it as the four .phase-tab controls falling back to their own 0px corner once the strip wraps at 390. They do not: the parent still has gap:0 and the tabs still have border-radius:0, so R3's joined-group test reads them as ONE BAR at both widths - they were never the fourth silhouette. Re-measured by replicating R3's own roleOf/shapeV against the page root at 390: pill->select(20), 8px->press(12), bar->navigate(4), 0px->press(6). The fourth silhouette is the six .kpi-toggle expanders - Availability, MTBF, MTTR, PM Compliance Rate, Downtime Pareto, Failure Frequency - wearing a square corner while the page's twelve other press controls (refresh-btn, details-toggle, showall-toggle) wear 8px. It is NOT a responsive defect: the toggle is 308px inside a 352px card (87.5%), just under isCardAnatomy's 90% cut-off, and at desktop it crosses that line and is excluded, which is the only reason R3 read 100% at 1280. The inconsistency existed at every width; one width could see it. Fixed by giving .kpi-toggle var(--wh-radius-sm) - the border and tint come from a JS-written inline style that sets no radius, so the class rule wins. Verified at BOTH widths: pill/8px/bar, 3 shapes for 3 roles, 0 collisions, R3 100%, analytics 100%. A mechanism must be measured, not inferred from the one thing that visibly changed.

W374/W375/W376/W3632/W3633 — J30, the ENERGY AUDIT journey in ENGLISH on PHONE-390, entry SEARCH-ARRIVAL, walked as a SOLO OWNER: an RA 11285 article -> the learn index -> the calculators guide -> the load-estimation calculator -> engineering-design -> project-manager -> project-report -> report-sender. Eight pages, four public and four behind the door. The public half was walked genuinely ANONYMOUS (signed out, every wh_* key cleared); the member half as jun.vanowner@workhive.test, Jun Salvador, "a one-person technician who owns his van and no hive", session verified through getDb().auth.getSession(). 390x845 CSS per survey, each page graded only after its text length held steady across three consecutive reads, each lens installed on a FRESH page load (install:true on all eight). 720 dims graded. THIS WALK FOUND THE DOOR LOCKED FROM THE INSIDE, AND THE PRODUCT HAD ALREADY BUILT THE KEY. Signed in and session-verified, Jun was redirected off engineering-design, project-manager, project-report, report-sender, asset-hub, logbook AND hive to index.html?signin=1, where a modal read "Sign in to open Eng. Design." over a Username/Password form whose only alternative was "Don't have an account? Create one for free". He HAD an account. He was signed into it. A second one would have landed in exactly the same place - and hive.html, the one page that could have given him a hive, sat behind the same gate. A closed loop for a persona the platform's own RLS SOLO branches, its solo seeder and its roadmap all treat as first-class. THE MECHANISM, CONFIRMED IN CODE AND THROUGH JUN'S OWN TOKEN. utils.js restoreIdentityFromSession resolves the person through v_worker_truth, which carries ONE ROW PER HIVE MEMBERSHIP. Read as Jun: 0 rows. So WORKER_NAME comes back empty and every page gating on it redirects. The multi-hive end of this same view was fixed months ago (two rows broke .maybeSingle()); this is the other end, ZERO rows, and it had never been walked because nobody hive-less could sign in until the solo personas were seeded three days ago. That earlier J11 attempt concluded "it is the cast, not the product" - correctly, then, because the cast could not authenticate at all. With a person who CAN sign in, the same eight pages give the opposite answer. WHY IT STAYED INVISIBLE. index.html's Create Account writes localStorage wh_last_worker on success, so the cache carries the person on the device the account was made on. The bounce only appears on a SECOND device, in a private window, or after storage is cleared - the same "the bounce warms the cache so it never looks reproducible" shape the file's own comment records for multi-hive users. Every reading in this walk was taken with wh_last_worker DELETED immediately before the navigation, so none of it is the cache answering. FIXED BY READING THE ROW THE PRODUCT'S OWN SIGN-UP WRITES. worker_profiles is keyed on auth_uid, not on membership, and Create Account inserts username + display_name into it; index.html's own comment says a brand-new account with no membership "stays in solo mode". restoreIdentityFromSession now falls back to that row when the membership view is empty - deactivated_at honoured, so a closed profile restores nothing - and then to the session's user_metadata, which is where the GoTrue admin API personas carry their name. One extra REST call ONLY when the membership lookup already came back empty, so the hive-member path is untouched. VERIFIED WITH A COLD CACHE ON EVERY PAGE. All four member pages render for Jun: engineering-design 96%, project-manager 100%, project-report 100%, report-sender 100%, each with hive=null and worker="Jun Salvador" resolved from the session rather than from storage. And hive.html now reaches the empty state it always had: "Join or create a team to share work, see who's active, and track your hive's jobs in real time." with Create a Hive and Join with Code. That door was built. It was simply unreachable by the only people who needed it. sw.js v356 -> v357 (utils.js is shell). THE PUBLIC HALF IS THE PROGRAM'S FIRST FULL-RUBRIC READING OF LEARN AND CALCULATOR PAGES, and it is where the remaining findings are. tools/load-estimation-calculator reads 100%. learn/index reads 97%. The two long-form articles read 90% and 85% and carry the heaviest cluster in this walk: B3 0% on both, with 37 sentences over twenty words on the RA 11285 checklist and 18 on the calculators guide, worst cases of 38 and 62 words. That is a CONTENT question, not a control question, and it is recorded here rather than rewritten - a 15,866-character compliance article is a different artifact from a tile subtitle, and deciding the bar for it is a judgement about the audience, not a bug fix. FOUR SMALLER ONES ON THE PUBLIC HALF ARE UNAMBIGUOUS AND WORTH THEIR OWN PASS: C2 99% on the calculators guide with a worst contrast of 1.11:1 on "Open Engineering Des..." - text that is effectively invisible; V1 0% with two content blocks overlapping at 390 ("Skill matrix" x "Digital logb"); D1 0% on both index-style pages, one icon-only control with no accessible name; and G1/I2 0% on both articles, no status region and no reserved block. K2/F1 report under-44 targets on both. engineering-design's own four findings are the standing supervisor-side shape: G3 0% (14 controls, 3 primary CTAs), A3 75%, R3 67% with a pill worn by both a press and a select - SAME-SHAPE-DIFFERENT-JOB - and N1 75% in English. The five rows differ only in which hive's data sits behind the same screens. This walk is the exception that proves the axis: it observed NO hive at all, because its person has none.
