THIS WALK FOUND THE DOOR LOCKED FROM THE INSIDE, AND THE PRODUCT HAD ALREADY BUILT THE KEY. Signed in and session-verified, Jun was redirected off engineering-design, project-manager, project-report, report-sender, asset-hub, logbook AND hive to index.html?signin=1, where a modal read "Sign in to open Eng. Design." over a Username/Password form whose only alternative was "Don't have an account? Create one for free". He HAD an account. He was signed into it. A second one would have landed in exactly the same place - and hive.html, the one page that could have given him a hive, sat behind the same gate. A closed loop for a persona the platform's own RLS SOLO branches, its solo seeder and its roadmap all treat as first-class. THE MECHANISM, CONFIRMED IN CODE AND THROUGH JUN'S OWN TOKEN. utils.js restoreIdentityFromSession resolves the person through v_worker_truth, which carries ONE ROW PER HIVE MEMBERSHIP. Read as Jun: 0 rows. So WORKER_NAME comes back empty and every page gating on it redirects. The multi-hive end of this same view was fixed months ago (two rows broke .maybeSingle()); this is the other end, ZERO rows, and it had never been walked because nobody hive-less could sign in until the solo personas were seeded three days ago. That earlier J11 attempt concluded "it is the cast, not the product" - correctly, then, because the cast could not authenticate at all. With a person who CAN sign in, the same eight pages give the opposite answer. WHY IT STAYED INVISIBLE. index.html's Create Account writes localStorage wh_last_worker on success, so the cache carries the person on the device the account was made on. The bounce only appears on a SECOND device, in a private window, or after storage is cleared - the same "the bounce warms the cache so it never looks reproducible" shape the file's own comment records for multi-hive users. Every reading in this walk was taken with wh_last_worker DELETED immediately before the navigation, so none of it is the cache answering. FIXED BY READING THE ROW THE PRODUCT'S OWN SIGN-UP WRITES. worker_profiles is keyed on auth_uid, not on membership, and Create Account inserts username + display_name into it; index.html's own comment says a brand-new account with no membership "stays in solo mode". restoreIdentityFromSession now falls back to that row when the membership view is empty - deactivated_at honoured, so a closed profile restores nothing - and then to the session's user_metadata, which is where the GoTrue admin API personas carry their name. One extra REST call ONLY when the membership lookup already came back empty, so the hive-member path is untouched. VERIFIED WITH A COLD CACHE ON EVERY PAGE. All four member pages render for Jun: engineering-design 96%, project-manager 100%, project-report 100%, report-sender 100%, each with hive=null and worker="Jun Salvador" resolved from the session rather than from storage. And hive.html now reaches the empty state it always had: "Join or create a team to share work, see who's active, and track your hive's jobs in real time." with Create a Hive and Join with Code. That door was built. It was simply unreachable by the only people who needed it. sw.js v356 -> v357 (utils.js is shell). W377/W378/W379/W3641/W3642 — the SOLO OWNER's project round in ENGLISH on PHONE-390: engineering-design -> project-manager -> project-report -> analytics. jun.vanowner@workhive.test, Jun Salvador, "a one-person technician who owns his van and no hive", session verified through getDb().auth.getSession(). 390x845 CSS per survey, each page graded only after its text length held steady across three consecutive reads, each lens installed on a FRESH page load (install:true on all four). 360 dims graded, 4 sub-100.

THIS IS THE FIRST WALK ON THE OTHER SIDE OF THE DOOR. Hours earlier this same cast was redirected off all four of these pages to a sign-in wall, because utils.js resolved identity through v_worker_truth, a view keyed on hive MEMBERSHIP, and a person with no hive returns zero rows from it. That is fixed - the resolver now falls back to worker_profiles, which is keyed on auth_uid and which the product's own Create Account writes, then to the session's user_metadata - and every reading here was taken with wh_last_worker DELETED immediately before the navigation, so none of it is a warm cache answering. worker="Jun Salvador" on all four, hive=null on all four.

THE FIX'S PRIMARY LEG IS NOW EXERCISED, NOT ASSUMED. Jun carries his name in user_metadata and has no worker_profiles row, so the four readings above prove only the metadata leg. A reversible probe proved the other: inserting a worker_profiles row for Jun through HIS OWN token and reloading with a cold cache resolved wh_last_worker to "Jun Salvador (probe)" - the display_name - which is the leg a real signed-up solo owner travels. The row was then deleted and audited: 0 probe rows, 0 rows for Jun, back to the exact prior state.

THAT PROBE ALSO SETTLED WHETHER analytics' "Unavailable" IS A PRODUCT DEFECT. IT IS NOT. As seeded, Jun's analytics reads 1,237 characters and the OEE tile says "Unavailable", because analytics-orchestrator refuses him 403 "No worker profile for caller" - and it is right to, because the seeder created him through the GoTrue admin API without the worker_profiles row the product's own sign-up always writes. WITH that row present the same page computed real KPIs: 5,935 characters, PM compliance 0%, OEE "No logbook data found". So the 403 is a gap in tools/seed_solo_personas.py, not in the platform, and the solo personas are not yet faithful stand-ins for a real solo owner. Recorded rather than reported as a finding - the difference is the probe.

engineering-design CARRIES ALL FOUR FINDINGS and they are the standing supervisor-side shape, unchanged by who is looking: G3 0% (14 controls, 3 primary CTAs), A3 75% (primaryCta=3/2, one disclosure, four blocks), R3 67% with a pill worn by BOTH a press and a select - SAME-SHAPE-DIFFERENT-JOB, which is component vocabulary rather than layout - and N1 75% in ENGLISH, more evidence that N1 is not a Filipino artifact.

project-manager, project-report and analytics all read 100%. They read 100% for a person who has nothing in them yet, which is the harder case: each renders an empty state rather than a wall.

ONE MORE THING THE PROBE FOUND, recorded because silence is the part that matters: worker_profiles accepts an INSERT from its owner and returns 0 rows for their DELETE, with no error. The row could not be removed through Jun's own token and needed the owner connection. A profile that a person cannot delete is a defensible design; a delete that reports success while changing nothing is the fourth state a reader misreads as fact.

The five rows differ only in which hive's data sits behind the same screens. This walk, like the energy-audit walk before it, observed NO hive at all. W380/W381/W382/W3650/W3651 — the WORKER'S DAY in ENGLISH on PHONE-390: alert-hub -> dayplanner -> logbook -> analytics -> report-sender. bryangarcia@auth.workhiveph.com, Bryan Garcia, wh_hive_role=worker in Baguio Textile Mills, session verified through getDb().auth.getSession() AND wh_hive_name re-read after a member page load. 390x845 CSS per survey, each page graded only after its text length held steady across three consecutive reads, each lens installed on a FRESH page load (install:true on all five). 450 dims graded, 3 sub-100.

THE FIRST ATTEMPT AT THIS WALK WAS DISCARDED, AND WHY IS WORTH MORE THAN THE WALK. I signed Bryan in with signInWithPassword and went straight to alert-hub, having cleared every wh_* key. The session was valid and getDb().auth.getSession() said so, so the walk looked properly cast - but wh_hive_id was never written, because the product resolves membership during ITS OWN sign-in flow and I had bypassed the front door. Five pages were surveyed in a state no real person is ever in: a hive MEMBER rendering as though he had no hive. The numbers say how large the error was: alert-hub 462 characters against 5,146, analytics "Avg across 4 assets" against "Avg across 16", report-sender 1,250 against 1,978. Three of the five still read 100% and would have banked without complaint. v_worker_truth read through Bryan's own token showed the membership was there the whole time (hive_id 084c113b), so nothing was broken except my method. The surveys were deleted, hive.html was loaded until wh_hive_name appeared, and every page was walked again. A HARNESS THAT SKIPS THE PRODUCT'S OWN SIGN-IN SIDE EFFECTS GRADES A STATE THAT DOES NOT EXIST, and a page reading 100% is not evidence that the page was the one you meant to grade.

THE CORRECTED WALK IS QUIET AND ITS TWO FINDINGS ARE BOTH R3, ON DIFFERENT OWNERS. alert-hub R3 67% - one card treatment, four control silhouettes (12px, bar, pill, 8px) for three roles - is the component-vocabulary one: it reads the same at 1280 and at 390 on every walk that has touched it. analytics R3 67% is C-J, the phase-tab strip wrapping into a 2x2 grid at phone width, which appears at 390 and not at 1280. Same dim, two mechanisms, and it is the pair of walks that tells them apart. analytics' N1 75% rides alongside in ENGLISH, which is again the plain evidence that N1 is not a Filipino artifact.

dayplanner, logbook and report-sender all read 100%. logbook does so on the corrected lens, where its 45 seeded work-history entries are excluded as the worker-authored content they are. report-sender reads 100% with the heading that used to be recomposed in JS from English literals.

analytics' OEE tile reads "Avg across 16 assets" here - a computed number, not the empty state - so the C-N branch fixed this morning correctly does NOT fire in a hive that has quality readings. The fleet hive, which has none, is the one that meets that sentence.

The five rows differ only in which hive's data sits behind the same screens; this walk observed Baguio Textile Mills. Surveyed: alert-hub 90 dims, 1 sub-100 | analytics 90 dims, 2 sub-100 | dayplanner 90 dims, 0 sub-100 | logbook 90 dims, 0 sub-100 | report-sender 90 dims, 0 sub-100. [2026-09-11] RETRACTED (interpretation only - the measurement stands): R3 - "analytics: R3 67% - cardTreatments=1 · silhouettes=4 for 3 role(s) (pill,8px,bar,0px)". The NUMBER is right and the STORY told about it was wrong. Every note carrying this finding explained it as the four .phase-tab controls falling back to their own 0px corner once the strip wraps at 390. They do not: the parent still has gap:0 and the tabs still have border-radius:0, so R3's joined-group test reads them as ONE BAR at both widths - they were never the fourth silhouette. Re-measured by replicating R3's own roleOf/shapeV against the page root at 390: pill->select(20), 8px->press(12), bar->navigate(4), 0px->press(6). The fourth silhouette is the six .kpi-toggle expanders - Availability, MTBF, MTTR, PM Compliance Rate, Downtime Pareto, Failure Frequency - wearing a square corner while the page's twelve other press controls (refresh-btn, details-toggle, showall-toggle) wear 8px. It is NOT a responsive defect: the toggle is 308px inside a 352px card (87.5%), just under isCardAnatomy's 90% cut-off, and at desktop it crosses that line and is excluded, which is the only reason R3 read 100% at 1280. The inconsistency existed at every width; one width could see it. Identity survived every hop; every surface rendered (logbook 369,155 chars, report-sender 134,314, analytics-report 121,529, project-report 88,920, audit-log 87,477). 450 dims graded across five surfaces.

THIS ROW BANKS ZERO FINDINGS, AND THAT IS A CLAIM ABOUT THE PRODUCT AS IT NOW STANDS, NOT ABOUT WHAT THE WALK MET. The walk found four sub-100 dims. Three were real and were FIXED and re-verified in the same session, on the same live pages; one was the instrument being wrong and the ruler was corrected. Nothing was waved through.

FIXED IN THE PRODUCT. (1) report-sender F1/K2: the Remove control on a saved recipient chip was 28x28, the smallest target on the page and the only destructive one - a destructive control is the last that should be hard to hit accurately. The chip is 65px tall with a 45px content box, so .contact-delete went to 44x44 with the chip unchanged at 321x65 (measured before and after). (2) audit-log R1: the root read gaps=[14,16] and the off-scale 14 was the SHARED .wh-help "How this page works" disclosure, whose margin-bottom is 14px against a declared scale of 4/8/12/16/24/32 (tokens.css) - so the one off-scale gap on this page was on all 30 pages carrying the block. Changed to 16px in BOTH copies in one edit: components.css and the utils.js fallback rule, which carries a standing note that the two must stay byte-identical because a second, DIFFERENT rule arriving after first paint was itself a measured layout shift. audit-log re-read 16px computed and R1 100%.

CORRECTED IN THE INSTRUMENT. report-sender graded J1 0% - "1 destructive control(s)" unguarded, which the severity scale turns into a BLOCKER. It was false: deleteContact() opens window.whConfirm() before touching anything and refuses outright when offline. The lens missed it because BOTH of its routes were closed - the button is addEventListener-wired (no onclick attribute) and template-rendered with no id (it is keyed by data-del), so the id-anchored source scan never ran. The dim's own comment says a slip-guard is "a MECHANISM, not an attribute spelling", and anchoring on the ID was that same error one level up. J1 now also anchors on a DISTINCTIVE class (>=6 chars, <=8 occurrences, so a generic token like "btn" can never qualify) and follows the handler ONE HOP: the code beside the anchor calls deleteContact(...), and that function's own source carries the guard. Calibrated against a false pass it initially produced - the wide window let the CONTAINER class contact-chip inherit the guard of the delete wiring rendered a few lines away, which would excuse a control that merely sits near a guarded one - so the hop window is tighter than the direct-text window (-60/+300 vs -300/+800). Measured after: the real .contact-delete resolves (hop:deleteContact), contact-chip and an invented class do not.

WHAT THIS WALK SAW THAT A BOARD AT REST CANNOT. Every one of the three product defects lives in a state a signed-in fleet supervisor reaches on a phone: a rendered recipient chip, a disclosure block above real content, a guarded delete wired at render time. And the J1 error is the standing lesson again - the instrument was wrong more often than the code, so a blocker is verified against the element before it is believed. THE FIRST ALL-CLEAN WALK OF THE PROGRAM, AND ITS CELL IS THE POINT. Five pages, 450 dims, no finding. That is a real result rather than a shallow one - every survey carries a settle receipt, a fresh lens install and its own viewport - but it should be read for WHICH cell produced it: an English-reading supervisor on a wide screen is the best-supported combination this platform has, and it is the combination most like the people who built it. Set beside the same day's Filipino phone-worker walks, which produced findings on every path, the shape of the platform's real gap is visible: it is strongest for the reader it was written in and thinnest for the worker it was written for.

That contrast is only trustworthy because the ruler was fixed first. Until today four of the rubric's vocabularies read English only - the readability grade, the freshness words, the guidance verbs and the permission wall - and each made the Filipino side look worse than it was. Some of the earlier gap was the instrument. What remains after the correction is the honest difference, and it is smaller than the bank said this morning.

THE ROLE CONTRAST IS THE SECOND HALF OF THE AUDIT-LOG STORY. The worker walk earlier today met #gate-not-supervisor and a locked card, 425 characters, and the rubric now correctly returns E3/G1/I2 as N/A for that persona. Rosa meets no gate at all - gateVisible=false, 2,766 characters of actual log - and the same three dims are MEASURED and pass. One page, one filename, two entirely different screens, and both now graded as what they are. A page's score is a claim about ONE persona in ONE auth state; this pair is the evidence for that rule rather than a restatement of it.

W390/W391/W392/W3669/W3670 — the FLEET SUPERVISOR's BENCHMARK round in ENGLISH on PHONE-390: hive -> analytics -> ph-intelligence -> analytics -> community. This is J21's shape, the federated-benchmark story: read your own board, read your own numbers, read them against the national picture, then take the finding to the community. Rosa dela Cruz, delacruzfleet@auth.workhiveph.com, wh_hive_role=supervisor in Dela Cruz Delivery Fleet, session verified through getDb().auth.getSession() AND wh_hive_name polled until non-null after a member page load, so the cast is a hive MEMBER rather than a valid session with no hive behind it. 390x845 CSS per survey, each page graded only after its text length held steady across three consecutive reads, each lens installed on a FRESH page load. 360 dims graded, 5 sub-100. analytics is walked twice in this path and is the same surface in the same state both times, so it is surveyed once.

THE C-N FIX HOLDS IN THE HIVE THAT FOUND IT. analytics reads 99% here with R3 and N1 and NO B3 finding - the passive OEE sentence that scored this page B3 67% this morning, in this same fleet hive, is gone, and the tile now names the half that is actually missing. That is the fix confirmed on a second cast in the hive whose data produced it.

hive CARRIES THE STANDING SUPERVISOR CLUSTER, and this is the axis it keeps proving: G3 0% (25 controls, 3 primary CTAs) with A3 75% (primaryCta=3/2, eight disclosures, twelve blocks). Every G3/A3 reading on this page has come from a supervisor cast and none from a worker cast, which is what scoped C-G's fix to the supervisor's board rather than to the page. Its third finding is C1 67% - three big sizes across eleven distinct steps - a type-scale observation rather than a control one.

hive also reports h2Visible=3 of 10, the data-gated outline: Dela Cruz is busy enough to earn three of its ten headings where the quiet Baguio hive renders none and reads A2 50%. Same page, same lens, two hives, and the difference is entirely in what the hive has done.

ph-intelligence AND community BOTH READ 100%. ph-intelligence does so at 801 characters - it is the opt-in national view and a fleet that has not opted in meets a short honest page rather than a wall. community reads 100% carrying the author-delete spacing fix from earlier in this program.

The five rows differ only in which hive's data sits behind the same screens; this walk observed Dela Cruz Delivery Fleet. Surveyed: analytics 90 dims, 2 sub-100 | community 90 dims, 0 sub-100 | hive 90 dims, 3 sub-100 | ph-intelligence 90 dims, 0 sub-100. [2026-09-11] RETRACTED (interpretation only - the measurement stands): R3 - "analytics: R3 67% - cardTreatments=1 · silhouettes=4 for 3 role(s) (pill,8px,bar,0px)". The NUMBER is right and the STORY told about it was wrong. Every note carrying this finding explained it as the four .phase-tab controls falling back to their own 0px corner once the strip wraps at 390. They do not: the parent still has gap:0 and the tabs still have border-radius:0, so R3's joined-group test reads them as ONE BAR at both widths - they were never the fourth silhouette. Re-measured by replicating R3's own roleOf/shapeV against the page root at 390: pill->select(20), 8px->press(12), bar->navigate(4), 0px->press(6). The fourth silhouette is the six .kpi-toggle expanders - Availability, MTBF, MTTR, PM Compliance Rate, Downtime Pareto, Failure Frequency - wearing a square corner while the page's twelve other press controls (refresh-btn, details-toggle, showall-toggle) wear 8px. It is NOT a responsive defect: the toggle is 308px inside a 352px card (87.5%), just under isCardAnatomy's 90% cut-off, and at desktop it crosses that line and is excluded, which is the only reason R3 read 100% at 1280. The inconsistency existed at every width; one width could see it. Fixed by giving .kpi-toggle var(--wh-radius-sm) - the border and tint come from a JS-written inline style that sets no radius, so the class rule wins. Verified at BOTH widths: pill/8px/bar, 3 shapes for 3 roles, 0 collisions, R3 100%, analytics 100%. A mechanism must be measured, not inferred from the one thing that visibly changed.

J5-shaped buyer journey, walked step by step through chrome-devtools-mcp: marketplace -> marketplace-seller -> analytics -> audit-log, phone-390 mobile+touch, English, normal conditions, present moment, cast as Rosa dela Cruz, supervisor of Dela Cruz Delivery Fleet, signed in through the platform's own wall. Deliberately NOT a marketplace platform admin: that table holds exactly two names, Leandro Marquez and Pablo Aguilar, and both were checked and avoided, because an admin cast sees surfaces a buyer never does. Identity survived every hop; marketplace 354,842 chars, marketplace-seller 234,900, analytics 215,139, audit-log 87,477. 360 dims graded.

THE FINDING THIS WALK EXISTS FOR: THE TABS HAD NO NAMES ON A PHONE. marketplace graded D1 0% - "0/1 icon-only controls named". Looking at the control rather than the number showed the defect was four times larger than the dim reported AND present on a second page. At phone width both pages hide their tab text with `display:none` (marketplace `.section-tab .tab-label` under 400px; marketplace-seller `.tab-btn span.lbl` under 480px), and display:none does not merely hide an element - it removes it from the ACCESSIBILITY TREE. The icon beside each label is aria-hidden="true", so the accessible name of each tab collapsed to whatever was left, its count. On marketplace a screen reader announced the four primary marketplace sections as "9, tab", "5, tab", "6, tab" and "—, tab". On marketplace-seller, Listings and Inquiries both announced as "0", while Analytics and Services did not - they carry an aria-label, so someone had already met this bug and fixed the two tabs in front of them. That is the partial-fix shape again: the same defect, one page over, left standing.

WHY THE RULER SAW ONLY ONE OF THE EIGHT. D1's icon-only test is `innerText` symbol-only, and it reads the DATA rather than the CONTROL: "9", "5", "6" and "0" all contain a word character, so those tabs never qualified; only Services, whose count renders as an em dash, matched. marketplace-seller's Analytics tab has no count at all, so its innerText is EMPTY - also not symbol-only, also invisible to the dim. One dash-shaped count is the whole reason this was found, on a page where seven other tabs had the same fault. The dim is left as it is here and the finding recorded instead, because tightening it to catch a count-only accessible name is a change to D1's definition, not a bug in its implementation.

FIXED, on both pages, with the clip pattern (.sr-only in wh-tw.css): the label is taken out of the visual flow by absolute positioning so it contributes no width, and stays in the a11y tree. Verified live and measured before/after, because a layout change here would have traded one defect for another: marketplace tab widths 80/79/79/82 before and 80/79/79/82 after, names now "Parts 9 / Training 5 / Hiring 6 / Services —"; marketplace-seller 83/82/82/82 with names "Listings 0 / Inquiries 0 / Analytics / Services 0". marketplace re-read D1 N/A ("no icon-only controls in this state") and 100% overall. The two existing aria-labels on the seller tabs are left in place and simply win the name computation.

BANKED, NOT FIXED, AND ON PURPOSE: marketplace-seller G3 0% / A3 75% (15 controls, 4 primary CTAs against a threshold of 2). The four are the header "Post a listing", "Save" on the profile name, "Save certifications", and the empty-state "Post a Listing". The redundancy between the first and last is real and worth a design decision. It is NOT taken here, because the fourth CTA is the empty state's own recovery path - deleting it to satisfy G3 would manufacture exactly the dead end X1 exists to catch, which is trading a measured dim for an unmeasured one. This is a hierarchy question for a person, so it stays in the bank as a finding with its reasoning rather than being quietly resolved by removing a useful control.

audit-log came through at 100% for this persona, confirming the shared .wh-help spacing fix made earlier in the session holds across a second cast. analytics' four (B3 67% passive voice, R3 67% card treatments, N1 75% data-i label coverage, C2 98% worst 4.18:1) are the standing measurements already verified genuine today. Surveyed: analytics 90 dims, 4 sub-100 | audit-log 90 dims, 0 sub-100 | marketplace-seller 90 dims, 2 sub-100 | marketplace 90 dims, 0 sub-100. [2026-09-11] RETRACTED (interpretation only - the measurement stands): R3 - "analytics: R3 67% - cardTreatments=1 · silhouettes=4 for 3 role(s) (pill,8px,bar,0px)". The NUMBER is right and the STORY told about it was wrong. Every note carrying this finding explained it as the four .phase-tab controls falling back to their own 0px corner once the strip wraps at 390. They do not: the parent still has gap:0 and the tabs still have border-radius:0, so R3's joined-group test reads them as ONE BAR at both widths - they were never the fourth silhouette. Re-measured by replicating R3's own roleOf/shapeV against the page root at 390: pill->select(20), 8px->press(12), bar->navigate(4), 0px->press(6). The fourth silhouette is the six .kpi-toggle expanders - Availability, MTBF, MTTR, PM Compliance Rate, Downtime Pareto, Failure Frequency - wearing a square corner while the page's twelve other press controls (refresh-btn, details-toggle, showall-toggle) wear 8px. It is NOT a responsive defect: the toggle is 308px inside a 352px card (87.5%), just under isCardAnatomy's 90% cut-off, and at desktop it crosses that line and is excluded, which is the only reason R3 read 100% at 1280. The inconsistency existed at every width; one width could see it. Fixed by giving .kpi-toggle var(--wh-radius-sm) - the border and tint come from a JS-written inline style that sets no radius, so the class rule wins. Verified at BOTH widths: pill/8px/bar, 3 shapes for 3 roles, 0 collisions, R3 100%, analytics 100%. A mechanism must be measured, not inferred from the one thing that visibly changed.

J7 knowledge loop, walked step by step through chrome-devtools-mcp: community -> skillmatrix -> achievements -> public-feed -> logbook, phone-390 mobile+touch, English, normal conditions, present moment, as Romeo Beltran, a plain WORKER of Manila Electronics Assembly (deliberately not a supervisor and not a marketplace platform admin). Signed in through the platform's own wall; identity survived every hop. community 201,331 chars, logbook 380,836, skillmatrix 106,870, achievements 93,950, public-feed 61,639. 450 dims graded, and the walk closes with zero sub-100 dims - after the one defect it found was fixed at its SOURCE.

THE ONE FINDING, AND IT WAS A PLATFORM COLOUR CONTRACT, NOT A PAGE. logbook graded C2 92%: the category chips measured "Instrumentation" 4.09:1 and "Electrical" 4.2:1, and the open-jobs badge 4.38:1, all against the 4.5:1 that 10px-13px uppercase text owes under WCAG 1.4.3. This same finding had been banked from an earlier walk and verified genuine twice, so the question this time was not whether it was real but why it kept coming back.

It kept coming back because it was never a colour-picking problem. tokens.css already declares an AA-safe TEXT variant beside each fill - `--wh-red: #f87171; /* alert / danger fill (AA text = --wh-red-text) */`, plus --wh-blue-text, --wh-orange-text, --wh-violet-text - and every failing element was using the FILL token, or its literal, as TEXT. The contrast contract was written down and simply not adopted, the same shape as .wh-help and whListError before it.

FIXED AT THREE LEVELS, all verified live on the same pages:
  * logbook catColors + criticalityBadge: the badge text literals became var(--wh-blue-text), var(--wh-red-text), var(--wh-orange-text), var(--wh-violet-text). Pneumatic and Lubrication keep their literals on purpose - no -text token is declared for green or yellow and neither was an offender, so inventing one would be a palette decision rather than a contrast fix.
  * logbook's open-jobs count badge: color:var(--wh-red) -> var(--wh-red-text) at 10px.
  * utils.js renderKpiTile, the SHARED verdict chip: its red and yellow rows used var(--wh-red)/var(--wh-orange) as the label colour at 0.63rem, which is why analytics' "✗ Critical" chip measured 4.18:1 - on every page that renders a red KPI tile, not just the one that was walked. The grey row of that same palette had already been tuned for APCA on 2026-09-07 while red and yellow were left behind, which is the partial-fix shape this repo keeps rediscovering.

MEASURED AFTER, by the same oracle that failed them: logbook C2 100% - 208 of 208 text elements at or above their WCAG floor, ZERO offenders, whole page 100%. analytics C2 100% with zero offenders (its N1 and R3 remain and are unrelated). The fix is in the shared helper and in the page's own colour maps, so it reaches the surfaces this walk never opened.

WHAT THE WALK SAW THAT A BOARD AT REST CANNOT: this exact logbook C2 finding does NOT appear when logbook is walked as a fleet supervisor earlier in the same session - "Instrumentation" is an asset category in Manila Electronics' data and simply is not on the fleet's screens. Two walks of one file, two different scores, both correct: a page's score is a claim about ONE persona in ONE auth state, and the pair is the evidence. W3452/W3455/W3458/W3461/W3464/W3467/W3690 — the worker's growth-and-community round in ENGLISH on desktop-1280: community -> skillmatrix -> achievements -> public-feed -> logbook. bryangarcia@auth.workhiveph.com, hive Baguio Textile Mills, wh_hive_role=worker, session verified through getDb().auth.getSession(). 1280x860 CSS on every survey, each page graded only after its text length held steady across three consecutive reads. 450 dims graded. skillmatrix, achievements and public-feed had not been walked in this program.

THE PAGE ALREADY KNEW THE RULE AND APPLIED IT TO ONLY ONE OF ITS TWO DELETE BUTTONS. community scored Z3 95% - "3 crowded/small target(s) risk mis-tap: Delete my post(destructive)" x3. Reading the markup rather than guessing at the number found the shape exactly: community.html renders TWO different delete controls, and the MODERATOR's one carries an explicit style="margin-left:22px" - a deliberate separation, because it is destructive and must not sit flush against the control beside it. The AUTHOR's delete, the one every ordinary member meets on their own post, never got that separation. Measured live: 44x44 with a 4px horizontal gap, on all six instances, each scrolled into view and re-measured. The target SIZE was never the problem - it already meets the 44px floor - and the two controls sitting 4px apart are precisely the two most confusable on the surface: "Edit my post" and "Delete my post".

FIXED by giving the author's delete the page's OWN precedent value (22px) rather than inventing a new one, so both destructive controls on this surface now behave identically. Verified live: the gap reads 26px on every instance, Z3 goes 95% -> 100% ("all 59 targets clear the 24px + spacing floor"), and the page reads 100% overall. community.html is not a precached shell page, so no CACHE_NAME bump is owed. This is the paired-write family again - a safety rule applied to one side of a pair and not the other - and it is the second destructive control this program has had to widen, after report-sender's 28x28 Remove.

A CLAIM I NEARLY MADE AND THE EVIDENCE WITHDREW. The first measurement pass suggested the third delete button OVERLAPPED the full-width "Post to Hive" composer by 3px, which would have been a far more serious finding: a destructive control capturing clicks aimed at the primary submit. Scrolling it into view and re-measuring returned an overlap of ZERO, and an elementFromPoint probe could not test the original reading at all because those coordinates sat below the fold. Two readings that disagree are not a finding, so no overlap is claimed - what survives is the 4px gap, which reproduced identically on all six instances under a settled layout. The rubric's own verdict ("crowded", not "overlapping") was the accurate one.

THE ONE REMAINING FINDING. logbook B3 67% - 51 sentences, one above grade 8, no long sentences, no passive. This is an ENGLISH walk, so the readability grade applies and bites legitimately; the same page's Filipino grade is now withheld because Flesch-Kincaid is English-calibrated.

THE WALK FOUND A TAP-TARGET FIX THAT MADE TWO LINKS FIGHT OVER THE SAME 26 PIXELS. hive V1 0%, and this time the lens was right. The approval-queue sentence renders its destinations as inline links inflated to a 44px box - min-height:44px, line-height:44px, margin:-14px - inside a

whose line-height is 18px. The negative margin keeps the TEXT FLOW looking normal, and it does. The HIT AREAS are the problem: in a hive with enough to review the sentence wraps, and "Asset Hub" [196,4525,270,4569] and "2 shift briefings" [157,4543,264,4587] land on adjacent lines with their 44px boxes OVERLAPPING BY 26px across a 68px width - 54% of the smaller target. A tap in that band lands on whichever link paints last rather than the one under the finger. The accessibility fix made the page harder to use for exactly the person it was written for. Its "Inline" exception exempts a target "in a sentence or whose size is otherwise constrained by the line-height of non-target text" - and these are nine characters inside a 101-character line. The comfort belongs to the line-height, not to the anchor's box. They are now plain inline links, the same shape skillmatrix's Resume and voice-journal's mailto already use and which the rubric's own _inlineProse recognises and exempts. One in-motion MCP walk, banked onto 8 row(s) that share its cell, page path, language, condition and moment (they differ only in which hive's data sits behind the screens - see tools/critic_walk_groups.py). ADVERSARY walk, step by step through chrome-devtools-mcp: hive -> audit-log -> logbook -> public-feed -> achievements, phone-390 mobile+touch, English, normal conditions, present moment. Cast as Romeo Beltran, a plain WORKER of Manila Electronics Assembly - the honest adversary for this platform is not an outsider but a real member reaching for surfaces their role does not own. Deliberately NOT a marketplace platform admin: that table holds exactly two names, Leandro Marquez and Pablo Aguilar, both checked and avoided. Signed in through the platform's own wall; identity survived every hop. hive 402,964 chars, logbook 380,857, achievements 93,971, audit-log 85,214, public-feed 61,660. 450 dims graded.

WHAT THE ROLE GATES DID. hive: the supervisor-only approval queue is correctly HIDDEN for this worker (#approval-queue carries .hidden), so the card that shows a supervisor their pending decisions does not exist on a worker's board. audit-log: the read returns this worker nothing, and rather than the silent empty state that would read as "nothing ever happened" - the refused-read trap - the page renders an honest wall: a lock, "Supervisors only", and a sentence saying WHO can see it and WHY ("so they can review approval, rejection, and member-management decisions"), plus a way back. No foreign hive name (Lucena, Baguio, Dela Cruz, Ramos, Tan) appears anywhere in the rendered page. The product behaved correctly at every gate this walk touched.

AN INSTRUMENT ERROR THIS WALK FOUND AND FIXED: THE RUBRIC GRADED A PERMISSION WALL AS A DATA PAGE. audit-log first read 93% with three HARD ZEROS - E3 "NO source chip", G1 "no status region", I2 "no reserved/optimistic block" - while the SAME FILE walked as a supervisor read 100%. All three were false. A wall has no data surface, so it owes no provenance chip, no live-status region and no skeleton to reserve; asking it for them is the same error as asking a poster for a status region, which this rubric already exempts. It was about to recur on every role-gated page walked as a non-privileged persona - a whole persona class still in the queue.

FIXED ON THE MECHANISM, NOT A HEURISTIC - AND THE FIRST VERSION WAS THE WRONG ONE. The first attempt required the root's visible text to be under 700 characters. It worked (worker 295, supervisor 1,067) and was too thin a margin to trust: the same help sentence, "The audit log is visible to hive supervisors...", renders in BOTH states, so a supervisor whose log happened to be nearly empty could have slipped under the threshold and had three dims silently excused. The platform already marks this state structurally - <div id="gate-not-supervisor" class="gate-card">, alongside gate-no-hive and gate-card on alert-hub and project-manager - and that element is display:none until the gate actually blocks. The dim now keys on a VISIBLE gate card carrying permission vocabulary. Same rule as everywhere else in this file: a track holding a fill is a progress bar, an empty .wh-progress-slot is a declared gradient, grade the mechanism the product ships.

VERIFIED ON ALL THREE STATES, which is what makes it a fix rather than a loosening: worker audit-log, gate-not-supervisor VISIBLE -> E3/G1/I2 N/A with their reasons, 99%; worker hive, no gate card at all -> the same three MEASURED at 100%, 99%; supervisor audit-log, both gate cards present but NOT visible -> the same three MEASURED at 100%, page 100%. The exemption fires only where the wall actually paints.

A METHOD TRAP WORTH RECORDING, because it nearly produced a false "the fix did not work". Re-running the rubric on a page WITHOUT reloading it silently keeps the OLD ruler: the installer opens with `if (window.__RUBRIC && window.__RUBRIC._v === V) return {already:true}`, so re-eval'ing an edited source into a page that already has the lens installed is a NO-OP and the pre-edit closure keeps grading. The earlier verifications in this session were only correct because each one navigated first. Every survey banked in this walk was taken after a navigation and carries `install: true` - a fresh install, proven per page, not assumed. The four findings banked (audit-log B3 67% and A1 75% - the wall's own short copy - and hive A2 50% headings, N1 75% data-i coverage) were all read by that same final lens. Surveyed: achievements 90 dims, 0 sub-100 | audit-log 90 dims, 2 sub-100 | hive 90 dims, 2 sub-100 | logbook 90 dims, 0 sub-100 | public-feed 90 dims, 0 sub-100.

W3494/W3497/W3500/W3503/W3506/W3509/W3708 — the ADVERSARY walk in ENGLISH on desktop-1280: hive -> audit-log -> logbook -> public-feed -> achievements. Cast as bryangarcia@auth.workhiveph.com, a WORKER in Baguio Textile Mills, asking at every step what he can reach that is not his. No adversary had been cast in this program before. Session verified through getDb().auth.getSession(). 1280x860 CSS per survey, each page graded only after its text length held steady across three consecutive reads. 450 dims graded, 5 sub-100.

THE BOUNDARY HOLDS AT THE DATA LAYER, NOT ONLY AT THE GATE CARD - AND THE PROOF NEEDED TWO PEOPLE. Asking as the worker, with HIS OWN session and never an owner or service connection, both audit tables returned ZERO rows and NO error - including when explicitly asking for a hive that is not his (.neq('hive_id', mine)). Zero rows is not by itself evidence of anything: it reads identically whether RLS withheld the rows or the table is simply empty, and stopping there would have been a boundary claim resting on an ambiguity. The same query run as Rosa dela Cruz, supervisor of Dela Cruz Delivery Fleet, with HER own session, returns 20 rows of hive_audit_log and 0 rows from any other hive. So the table demonstrably holds rows, the worker's identical unscoped request returned none of them, and the supervisor who may read them sees only her own hive's. Two personas, two tokens, one query - that is what makes it a finding rather than an absence.

Two things follow. The gate card on audit-log is NOT the security boundary, it is the honest EXPLANATION of one that already holds underneath; a UI-only wall would have leaked here and did not. And the refusal is SILENT - 0 rows, no error - which is the fourth state a reader can misread as "there is nothing", so the page showing "Supervisors only" instead of an empty list is doing exactly the right thing. The same walk earlier today confirmed the rubric now scores that wall as N/A rather than three hard zeros.

An honest note on method: my FIRST probe queried a table called `audit_log` and came back PGRST205, "could not find the table in the schema cache". That is not evidence of a boundary - it is evidence of a wrong table name, and reporting it as a clean refusal would have been a false pass. The real names came from the page's own queries (hive_audit_log, ai_audit_log), which is where they should have come from first.

THE FIVE RUBRIC FINDINGS. hive A2 50% is the sharpest and it is structural: the busiest member surface renders NINE content blocks under a SINGLE heading, with no h2 or h3 beneath it, so nothing in the document outline tells a reader - or a screen reader - where one section ends and the next begins. hive N1 75% ("label coverage 2/3, data-i=94") is the mechanism census again, in ENGLISH, which is useful confirmation that N1 is not a Filipino artifact. audit-log B3 67% (one of three sentences above grade 8) and A1 75% (an h1 and one 26px tier, no CTA) are the locked card seen as prose and as layout - the whole of what this persona can read on that page. logbook B3 67%, one sentence above grade 8 across 51.

public-feed and achievements read 100%, with zero i18n orphans on all five pages.

[2026-09-10] RETRACTED and REMOVED (the measurement itself is false): B3 - "logbook: B3 67% - sentences=51 · >20w=0 · passive=0 · grade>8=1". B3 grades the PRODUCT's writing, not the user's - a rule this rubric already states and already enforces for voice-journal transcripts and community posts, on the ground that holding the app to an 8th-grade, 20-word bar for how a WORKER TALKS is a category error. One in-motion MCP walk, banked onto 6 row(s) that share its cell, page path, language, condition and moment (they differ only in which hive's data sits behind the screens - see tools/critic_walk_groups.py). W3709/W3710/W3711/W3712/W3713/W3714 — TIER D, THE FIRST WHOLE-LIFETIME WALK OF THE PROGRAM: one hive from its first day to its first departure, 17 pages, 8 layers, in ENGLISH on desktop-1280 as a fleet supervisor. index -> hive -> asset-hub -> logbook -> pm-scheduler -> alert-hub -> dayplanner -> report-sender -> analytics-report -> shift-brain -> analytics -> audit-log -> project-report -> ph-intelligence -> community -> public-feed -> achievements. Rosa dela Cruz, delacruzfleet@auth.workhiveph.com, session verified through getDb().auth.getSession(). 1280x860 CSS on every survey, every page graded only after its text length held steady across three consecutive reads, every lens installed on a FRESH page load. 1,530 dims graded, 8 sub-100.

THE MOMENTS NEEDED NO SEEDING, AND CHECKING THAT WAS THE FIRST STEP. The row asks for day-1 + month-3 + year-2, and the plan says the seeders stage each moment and reverse after. They did not need to: the hive ALREADY carries 1,862 days of history - 2021-09-16 to 2026-10-22, 3,666 logbook entries, read with this supervisor's own session - because the five-year synthetic history was seeded at build time. The moments are historical data already present, so the honest way to walk them is through the product's OWN time controls rather than by writing anything. No staging, no reversal, no seed-row audit owed. The unit was flagged as heavy in the queue and was not.

THE MOMENTS WERE ACTUALLY WALKED, with a receipt per window. analytics' period control was driven through all four windows and each RECOMPUTED: 30 days ("Saved snapshot, computed 32 min ago"), then 90, 180 and 365 each returning "Recomputed just now · Based on your logbook · last N days (rolling, ending now)". Rendered content changes with the window (1,943 -> 4,394 characters) and so do the figures - a numbers-only diff of the whole page confirms 90 != 180 != 365. Recorded because my FIRST comparison said the windows were identical: it used a KPI selector that matched nothing, so it compared two empty lists. A vacuous equality is not a finding; the selector-independent diff is what settled it.

★THE WALK'S REAL YIELD IS WHAT THE CORRECTED B3 LENS EXPOSED ON ENGLISH PAGES. Hours earlier B3's splitter was found to treat an HTML source newline as a sentence boundary, so hard-wrapped English markup was shredded into fragments that trivially passed. This is the first walk run entirely on the corrected lens, and pages that read 100% all program now report real defects:
  asset-hub B3 0% - ALL THREE checks fail on one screen: a 21-word sentence, a passive one ("No assets are flagged as critical."), and grade 10.6 on "Walk through your list below and mark the top 5 production-blocking assets as Critical: this drives where AI...".
  index B3 67% - grade 13.1 on "Closing the Execution, Skills, Intelligence, and Marketplace gaps that hold Filipino worke...". That is the FRONT DOOR, the sentence strangers meet first.
  public-feed B3 67% - the 24-word "Signing in takes you to your hive's board: what you post there appears on your team's board only, never here, unless you share it.", which its own markup wrapping had hidden.
None of this is new copy; it has been shipping all along, and the ruler could not see it because of how the HTML happens to be wrapped. This is the strongest confirmation of that fix and the clearest statement of what it cost to have it wrong.

THE STANDING CLUSTERS REPRODUCE. hive G3 0% (24 controls, 3 primary CTAs) and A3 75% again, now on a fifth axis, with h2Visible=3 of h2InDom=10 - Dela Cruz is busy enough to earn three of its ten headings, against ZERO in the quiet Baguio hive. alert-hub R3 67%, unchanged at desktop as at phone, so still a component-vocabulary problem rather than a responsive one. analytics N1 75% (the documented mechanism census) and its two passive sentences are the C-I server-composed English.

ELEVEN OF THE SEVENTEEN PAGES READ 100%, including the whole reporting spine (analytics-report, report-sender, project-report, audit-log) and the closing stretch (community, ph-intelligence, achievements).

★A REGISTRY DRIFT THIS WALK UNCOVERED, AND THE GUARD IS WHAT FOUND IT. I walked the path the TRAJECTORY declares - which includes project-manager and skillmatrix - and bank_critic_walk refused the bank, because the CRITIC row declares a different path: public-feed instead of those two. Checked across the whole registry: 332 of the 724 critic rows carrying a page list disagree with their trajectory's. The two lists INSIDE each trajectory (top-level `pages` and `journey.pages`) agree perfectly, 0 of 724, and critic_seed_missing.py copies the trajectory's list faithfully - so this is STALENESS, not a seeding bug: those critic rows were seeded from an earlier revision and the trajectories moved on. The cost is real and I paid it here: a walker who reads the trajectory (the natural source, since it holds the journey definition) walks pages the bank will refuse, and a walker who reads the critic row walks a path the trajectory no longer claims. This walk was re-scoped to the critic row's list, which is what the bank enforces, and project-manager and skillmatrix were set aside rather than banked against rows that do not declare them. The trajectory's version looks the more correct of the two on its face - a hive's whole year plausibly includes its projects and its people's skills - so the repair direction is to re-sync critic.pages FROM the trajectory, and it wants a gate so the drift cannot return silently.

The six rows differ only in which hive's data sits behind the same screens; this walk observed Dela Cruz Delivery Fleet. rows.clean_note:
One in-motion MCP walk, banked onto 6 row(s) that share its cell, page path, language, condition and moment (they differ only in which hive's data sits behind the screens - see tools/critic_walk_groups.py). W3709/W3710/W3711/W3712/W3713/W3714 — TIER D, THE FIRST WHOLE-LIFETIME WALK OF THE PROGRAM: one hive from its first day to its first departure, 17 pages, 8 layers, in ENGLISH on desktop-1280 as a fleet supervisor. index -> hive -> asset-hub -> logbook -> pm-scheduler -> alert-hub -> dayplanner -> report-sender -> analytics-report -> shift-brain -> analytics -> audit-log -> project-report -> ph-intelligence -> community -> public-feed -> achievements. Rosa dela Cruz, delacruzfleet@auth.workhiveph.com, session verified through getDb().auth.getSession(). 1280x860 CSS on every survey, every page graded only after its text length held steady across three consecutive reads, every lens installed on a FRESH page load. 1,530 dims graded, 8 sub-100.

THE MOMENTS NEEDED NO SEEDING, AND CHECKING THAT WAS THE FIRST STEP. The row asks for day-1 + month-3 + year-2, and the plan says the seeders stage each moment and reverse after. They did not need to: the hive ALREADY carries 1,862 days of history - 2021-09-16 to 2026-10-22, 3,666 logbook entries, read with this supervisor's own session - because the five-year synthetic history was seeded at build time. The moments are historical data already present, so the honest way to walk them is through the product's OWN time controls rather than by writing anything. No staging, no reversal, no seed-row audit owed. The unit was flagged as heavy in the queue and was not.

THE MOMENTS WERE ACTUALLY WALKED, with a receipt per window. analytics' period control was driven through all four windows and each RECOMPUTED: 30 days ("Saved snapshot, computed 32 min ago"), then 90, 180 and 365 each returning "Recomputed just now · Based on your logbook · last N days (rolling, ending now)". Rendered content changes with the window (1,943 -> 4,394 characters) and so do the figures - a numbers-only diff of the whole page confirms 90 != 180 != 365. Recorded because my FIRST comparison said the windows were identical: it used a KPI selector that matched nothing, so it compared two empty lists. A vacuous equality is not a finding; the selector-independent diff is what settled it.

★THE WALK'S REAL YIELD IS WHAT THE CORRECTED B3 LENS EXPOSED ON ENGLISH PAGES. Hours earlier B3's splitter was found to treat an HTML source newline as a sentence boundary, so hard-wrapped English markup was shredded into fragments that trivially passed. This is the first walk run entirely on the corrected lens, and pages that read 100% all program now report real defects:
  asset-hub B3 0% - ALL THREE checks fail on one screen: a 21-word sentence, a passive one ("No assets are flagged as critical."), and grade 10.6 on "Walk through your list below and mark the top 5 production-blocking assets as Critical: this drives where AI...".
  index B3 67% - grade 13.1 on "Closing the Execution, Skills, Intelligence, and Marketplace gaps that hold Filipino worke...". That is the FRONT DOOR, the sentence strangers meet first.
  public-feed B3 67% - the 24-word "Signing in takes you to your hive's board: what you post there appears on your team's board only, never here, unless you share it.", which its own markup wrapping had hidden.
None of this is new copy; it has been shipping all along, and the ruler could not see it because of how the HTML happens to be wrapped. This is the strongest confirmation of that fix and the clearest statement of what it cost to have it wrong.

THE STANDING CLUSTERS REPRODUCE. hive G3 0% (24 controls, 3 primary CTAs) and A3 75% again, now on a fifth axis, with h2Visible=3 of h2InDom=10 - Dela Cruz is busy enough to earn three of its ten headings, against ZERO in the quiet Baguio hive. alert-hub R3 67%, unchanged at desktop as at phone, so still a component-vocabulary problem rather than a responsive one. analytics N1 75% (the documented mechanism census) and its two passive sentences are the C-I server-composed English.

ELEVEN OF THE SEVENTEEN PAGES READ 100%, including the whole reporting spine (analytics-report, report-sender, project-report, audit-log) and the closing stretch (community, ph-intelligence, achievements).

★A REGISTRY DRIFT THIS WALK UNCOVERED, AND THE GUARD IS WHAT FOUND IT. I walked the path the TRAJECTORY declares - which includes project-manager and skillmatrix - and bank_critic_walk refused the bank, because the CRITIC row declares a different path: public-feed instead of those two. Checked across the whole registry: 332 of the 724 critic rows carrying a page list disagree with their trajectory's. The two lists INSIDE each trajectory (top-level `pages` and `journey.pages`) agree perfectly, 0 of 724, and critic_seed_missing.py copies the trajectory's list faithfully - so this is STALENESS, not a seeding bug: those critic rows were seeded from an earlier revision and the trajectories moved on. The cost is real and I paid it here: a walker who reads the trajectory (the natural source, since it holds the journey definition) walks pages the bank will refuse, and a walker who reads the critic row walks a path the trajectory no longer claims. This walk was re-scoped to the critic row's list, which is what the bank enforces, and project-manager and skillmatrix were set aside rather than banked against rows that do not declare them. The trajectory's version looks the more correct of the two on its face - a hive's whole year plausibly includes its projects and its people's skills - so the repair direction is to re-sync critic.pages FROM the trajectory, and it wants a gate so the drift cannot return silently.

The six rows differ only in which hive's data sits behind the same screens; this walk observed Dela Cruz Delivery Fleet.
